notes: Against the declared opposition of both patrician consuls, Marcius wins the censorship with tribunician aid — first plebeian censor; census itself instituted because debt payments had shifted much property.

quote: This year also had Marcus Fabius as dictator, not by reason of any terror of war, but in order that the Licinian law should not be observed at the consular elections
notes: Explicitly political dictatorship to defeat the Licinian law at the polls; Livy notes it proved no more effectual for the senators than at the censorial election.

quote: Lucius Furius Camillus being nominated dictator, Publius Cornelius Scipio being attached as master of the horse, restored to the patricians their former possession of the consulship
notes: Nominated to hold elections with both consuls ill; returns the consulship to the patricians and has himself elected — denounced by the commons (ch. 25) as the consulship taken as a bribe for infringing the Licinian law.

quote: with the approbation of the senate, he nominated Titus Manlius Torquatus dictator. The dictator, after appointing Aulus Cornelius Cossus his master of the horse, held the consular elections
notes: Election dictatorship during the stalled Greek maritime war; returns the 23-year-old Marcus Valerius Corvus (of the crow duel, same chapter) as consul in absentia.

quote: the interest of money from twelve was reduced to six per cent; and the payment of the debts was adjusted into equal portions of three years
notes: Interest halved (semiunciarium fenus) and debts rescheduled in instalments with a down payment; Livy notes public credit still outranked private distress in the senate's attention.

quote: Lucius Furius being created dictator, as if against all Latium already in arms, nominated Cneius Manlius Capitolinus his master of the horse
notes: Sudden Auruncan raid feared as concerted Latin war; justitium proclaimed, levy without exemptions; dictator vows the temple of Juno Moneta in battle and resigns on victory.

quote: it was resolved by the senate that a dictator should be nominated for the purpose of regulating the ceremonies. Publius Valerius Publicola was nominated
notes: After a rain of stones and daytime darkness following the Moneta dedication; supplications ordered for tribes and neighbouring states.

quote: Severe sentences of the people are said to have been passed on that year against usurers, for whom a day of trial had been appointed by the aediles
notes: Aedilician prosecutions of moneylenders before the people — enforcement arm of the book's interest-rate legislation.

quote: schemes were being formed in winter-quarters for taking away Capua from the Campanians by the same kind of wickedness as that by which they had taken it from its original possessors
notes: Garrison troops, envious of Campanian land and pressed by debt at home, plot to seize Capua; consul Marcius defuses by rumour of extended quarters, then purges the army by furloughs (ch. 39) — triggering the mutiny coded next.

quote: having torn up their standard, more under the influence of their own impetuosity than by the command of their general, they arrive in hostile array at the eighth stone
notes: Purged mutineers band at Lautulae, encamp under Alba, abduct the retired Titus Quinctius as forced leader, and march on Rome (342 BCE); Livy reports a variant tradition (ch. 42) with no dictator and Caius Manlius as leader; resolved by negotiation, not battle.

quote: that an army was coming to meet them, and that Marcus Valerius Corvus was nominated dictator against them, and Lucius Aemilius Mamercinus master of the horse
notes: Dictator chosen for his popularity with the soldiers; his conciliation speech (ch. 40) and Quinctius's submission end the confrontation without bloodshed.

quote: proposed to the people in the Peteline grove, that the secession should not be visited with chastisement on any of the soldiers
notes: Settlement package: amnesty for the secession, ban on reproaching it, military sacrata lex that no enrolled soldier's name be struck without consent, ban on ex-tribunes of soldiers serving as centurions (aimed at Salonius, who waived it); cavalry pay-cut demand refused.

quote: Lucius Genucius, tribune of the commons, proposed to the people, that no one should be allowed to practise usury
notes: Genucian package in some annalists: usury banned outright, no iteration of the same office within ten years, no two offices in one year, both consulships opened to plebeians; Livy infers from the scale of concessions that the revolt had no little strength, and flags that the ancient writers agree only that there was a mutiny and that it was settled.

quote: their leading men, in their several deliberations among themselves, secretly fomented the plan of a war with Rome
notes: Latin leaders secretly plan war while demanding political parity; intelligence reaches Rome through private friendship ties; issues in the Latin War. Borderline domestic (allied-league politics).

quote: the consuls being ordered to resign their office before the usual time, in order that the new consuls might be elected the sooner to meet so important a war
notes: Consuls ordered to abdicate early; religious scruple about curtailed-term elections produces an interregnum; Torquatus and Decius elected.

quote: One of the consuls must be selected out of Rome, the other out of Latium; an equal portion of the senate must be from both nations; we must be one people, one republic
notes: Formal Latin demand for shared consulship and senate seats, rejected with threats of violence in the senate-house; precipitates the Latin War. Demand is over office-sharing, hence honors-office.

quote: since either the authority of consuls is to be established by your death, or by your forgiveness to be for ever annulled
notes: Consul has his own son beheaded for fighting against orders after a victorious single combat; lawful exercise of imperium ('Manlian orders' remembered with horror); army obedience enforced.

quote: The rights of citizenship were granted to the Campanian horsemen; and that it might serve as a memorial, they hung up a brazen tablet in the temple of Castor at Rome
notes: Citizenship grant for loyalty in the Latin War, recorded on a bronze tablet (explicit documentary record); Campanian state ordered to pay them 450 denarii each yearly.

quote: nominated as dictator Lucius Papirius Crassus, who then happened to be praetor; by him Lucius Papirius Cursor was appointed master of the horse
notes: Dictator named for the Antiate war because consul Manlius was too ill to command.

quote: he neither ceased to criminate the patricians to the people, his colleague by no means interfering, because he himself also was a plebeian
notes: Consul denied a triumph behaves 'like a seditious tribuneship'; Livy says the scanty land distribution in the Latin and Falernian territory afforded the groundwork of the criminations.

quote: he passed three laws, most advantageous to the commons, and injurious to the nobility; one, that the orders of the commons should be binding on all the Romans
notes: Publilian laws: plebiscites binding, patrum auctoritas given before the centuriate vote, one censor to be plebeian; passed by a plebeian dictator nominated by his own colleague.

quote: To the Lanuvians the right of citizenship was granted, and the exercise of their religious rights was restored to them
notes: State-by-state settlement of Latium: differentiated citizenship grants; Veliternian senate deported beyond the Tiber and their land colonized; intermarriage, commerce and councils removed from the other Latins.

quote: A new colony was also sent to Antium, with this provision, that if the Antians desired to be enrolled as colonists, permission to that effect should be granted
notes: Antium colonized; its warships confiscated, prows decorating the new Rostra in the forum; Antians interdicted the sea but granted citizenship.

quote: when the augurs declared that he seemed to have been created under an informality, the dictator and the master of the horse laid down their office
notes: Dictatorship annulled on augural grounds — recurrent pattern of religious veto over emergency appointments in this book.

quote: when brought to trial, was buried alive at the Colline gate, on the right of the causeway, in the field of wickedness
notes: Vestal suspected for over-elegant dress, denounced by a slave, tried before the pontiffs and buried alive.

quote: Quintus Publilius Philo was the first of the plebeians elected praetor, being opposed by Sulpicius the consul, who refused to take any notice of him as a candidate
notes: First plebeian praetor elected over active consular obstruction; senate acquiesces having lost the same fight over the consulship.

quote: they appointed Kaeso Duilius, Titus Quinctius, and Marcus Fabius commissioners for conducting the colony and distributing the land
notes: 2,500 colonists decreed for Cales explicitly 'that they might anticipate, by an act of kindness, the wishes of the commons' — land distribution as preemptive concession; named triumviral commission (register-producing procedure).

quote: A scruple afterwards arose that they were elected under an informality: and they laid down their office; and because a pestilence followed, recourse was had to an interregnum
notes: Second vitiated dictatorship in three chapters; pestilence read as contamination of the auspices; interregnum of at least five interreges follows.

quote: the rumour of a Gallic war had the effect of a real outbreak, so that they were determined that a dictator should be nominated
notes: Dictator appointed on rumor alone; scouts then report total quiet — emergency machinery triggered by information failure.

quote: The same year the census was performed, and the new citizens were rated; on their account the Maecian and Scaptia tribes were added
notes: Censorial registration of the newly enfranchised; two new tribes created; Acerrans enfranchised by praetorian law — the census as the absorptive instrument for annexation.

quote: Their attendants being instantly seized, informed against a great number of matrons, of whom to the number of one hundred and seventy were condemned
notes: First poisoning investigation at Rome: informer granted public faith, two patrician women drink their own preparations and die, 170 matrons condemned; treated as prodigy.

quote: it was determined that a dictator should be nominated for the purpose of driving the nail
notes: Dictator clavi figendi causa, on annalistic precedent from the secessions, to restore minds 'distracted by discord'; abdicates immediately after the rite.

quote: ordering that Vitruvius should be kept in prison, until the return of the consul, and that he should then be beaten with rods, and put to death
notes: Fundanian noble with a house on the Palatine leads the Privernate revolt; executed after the triumph; house razed (Vacciprata), goods consecrated to Semo Sancus — confiscation-liquidation pattern as in the Maelius case.

quote: a proposal was laid before the people, that the freedom of the state should be granted to the Privernians
notes: After the famous liberty answer ('such as those deserve who deem themselves worthy of liberty'), enfranchisement replaces punishment — clemency argued as stability policy.

quote: The same year a colony of three hundred was sent to Anxur, and received two acres of land each
notes: Small maritime colony with a recorded per-colonist allotment (2 iugera) — quantitative distribution datum.

quote: except the sending of a colony to Fregellae, a district which had belonged to the Sidicinians, and afterwards to the Volscians
notes: Colony planted in territory the Samnites claimed (per 8:23 their chief stated grievance) — a distribution decision that becomes a casus belli.

quote: This distribution of meat intended as a return for favours shown on the trial, proved also the means of procuring him the honour of a public office
notes: Private meat distribution at his mother's funeral, read by contemporaries as repayment for his acquittal; wins the plebeian tribunate in absentia over candidates canvassing in person — textbook private-largesse-to-office mechanism (cf. Machiavelli Disc. III.28).

quote: that Publilius Philo, when his year of office should expire, might continue in command, as pro-consul, until the war with the Greeks should be finished
notes: First prorogation of imperium in Roman history, passed through the tribunes and people for siege continuity at Palaepolis; paired first-ever triumph after office (8:26).

quote: Who did not plainly perceive, that the dictator's being a plebeian, was the defect which the augurs had discovered?
notes: Plebeian dictator's election voided by augurs on an undiscoverable flaw; tribunes denounce the ruling as class politics; elections stalled through fourteen interreges — religious machinery as partisan veto.

quote: a vast number of people, moved by compassion for his early age, and indignation at his barbarous treatment, reflecting at the same time on their own lot and that of their children, flocked together into the forum
notes: Abuse of a bonded debtor triggers a mass demonstration at the senate-house; crowd displays the scourged youth to senators entering — grievance channeled into immediate legislation rather than secession.

quote: the consuls were commanded to propose to the people, that no person should be held in fetters or stocks, except convicted of a crime
notes: Abolition of debt-bondage (nexum): goods not body answerable for debt; Livy calls it 'a new era of liberty'; confined debtors released. The structural end of the Book 2-6 debt-crisis cycle.

quote: he nominated Lucius Papirius Cursor, the most celebrated general, by far, of any in that age
notes: Dictator appointed when the consul fell gravely ill mid-campaign; the appointment sets up the Papirius-Fabius collision.

quote: betook himself to the quarters of the veterans, who were already raising a commotion in the assembly: from them the uproar spread through the whole body
notes: Army nearly mutinies to shield Fabius from execution; lictors obstructed; night ends the confrontation — threat of collective disobedience without open revolt.

quote: Quintus Fabius, who fought contrary to the order of his commander, is not acquitted of guilt; but after being condemned as guilty, is granted as a boon to the Roman people
notes: Spans 8:30-8:35: master of horse wins a battle against the dictator's orders; capital proceedings pursued from camp to senate to rostra; father appeals to tribunes and people; dictator yields to supplication while asserting the principle — discipline conflict resolved entirely inside ordinary channels.

quote: the soldiers exerted no vigour; and designedly kept from conquering, in order to injure the reputation of their leader
notes: Passive mutiny: troops deliberately withhold victory from the hated dictator; resolved not by punishment but by his calculated conciliation (visiting the wounded) — reputation repaired, army then wins decisively.

quote: Marcus Flavius, a tribune of the commons, proposed, that punishment should be inflicted on those of the Tusculans, by whose advice and assistance the Veliternians and Privernians had made war on the Roman people
notes: Collective treason trial of an allied municipality before the tribes; mourning-dress supplication defeats the proposal in every tribe but the Pollia; the grudge recorded as persisting for centuries in voting behavior.

quote: an alarm, which happened in the night, suddenly roused the people from their sleep, in such a fright, that the Capitol and citadel, the walls and gates, were all filled with men in arms
notes: Nocturnal panic mobilization with no discoverable author or cause — included as an unrest datum (false-alarm class).

quote: Aulus Cornelius Arvina being made dictator, and Marcus Fabius Ambustus master of the horse, a levy being held with more than usual rigour
notes: Livy flags source conflict at 8:40: some authorities say the consuls ran this war and Cornelius was dictator only to start the games during the praetor's illness; he distrusts funeral panegyrics and false statue inscriptions.

actors: consuls T. Veturius and Sp. Postumius
quote: to nominate a dictator to preside at the elections. They nominated Quintus Fabius Ambustus, and as master of the horse Publius Aelius Paetus
notes: Post-Caudium paralysis: discredited consuls forced by senate decree to name an elections dictator; first pair irregularly appointed and replaced by M. Aemilius Papus and L. Valerius Flaccus.

actors: interreges Q. Fabius Maximus and M. Valerius Corvus
quote: the people being dissatisfied with all the magistrates of that year, an interregnum ensued
notes: Neither elections dictator held the comitia; popular distrust of all Caudine-year magistrates forced an interregnum before Publilius and Papirius were elected.

quote: Let us then be delivered up to them by the heralds, naked, and in chains
notes: Senate proceeding on the Caudine sponsio: Postumius himself proposes the surrender of the sureties to free the people of the obligation; spans 9:8-9:10.

quote: a protest was attempted for a time by Lucius Livius and Quintus Maelius, tribunes of the commons
notes: Tribunes (themselves sureties) protest the deditio; persuaded by Postumius's argument, they resign office and are surrendered with the rest (9:10).

quote: I here surrender these men into your hands
notes: Formal fetial deditio of the Caudine sureties at Caudium; Pontius refuses to accept it (9:11) and sends them back unhurt; legal-theatrical resolution of the sponsio crisis.

quote: having instituted an inquiry by whose means the revolt had taken place, scourged with rods and beheaded such as he found to be guilty
notes: Satricum (Roman citizens) had defected to the Samnites after Caudium; two internal factions compete in betraying the Samnite garrison back to Rome; judicial inquiry and executions follow.

quote: This year praefects first began to be created for Capua, and a code of laws was given to that nation, by Lucius Furius the praetor
notes: First praefecti Capuam Cumas, requested by Capua itself as remedy for intestine dissensions; Antium likewise then asked for laws and received the colony's patrons as law-givers.

quote: At Rome, two additional tribes were constituted, the Ufentine and Falerine
notes: Tribal structure expanded to 31; incorporation of new citizen territory into the voting system.

quote: delivered over the legions, not to the consuls elected by themselves, who were Spurius Nautius and Marcus Popillius, but to a dictator, Lucius Aemilius
notes: Outgoing consuls hand the army to a dictator rather than to their own elected successors — a politically pointed transfer of command.

quote: the war was thenceforward conducted by a dictator, Quintius Fabius
notes: Consuls Papirius (4th) and Publilius (4th) remain at Rome while a dictator runs the Saticula campaign; master of horse later killed attacking without the dictator's orders (9:22).

actors: consuls M. Poetelius and C. Sulpicius
quote: All those who were brought to Rome were beaten with rods in the forum, and beheaded
notes: 225 identified authors of Sora's revolt and the massacre of Roman colonists executed publicly at Rome 'to the great joy of the commons, whose interest it most highly concerned' — colonist security as a plebeian interest.

actors: twelve young nobles of Ausona, Minturnae and Vescia
quote: Certain young men, of the principal families, twelve in number, having conspired to betray their respective cities
notes: Non-Roman polity: aristocratic youth faction invites Roman force into their own wavering cities; ends in indiscriminate massacre and the near-destruction of the Ausonian nation though the charge of revolt was scarcely proved.

quote: the resolution was carried, that the colonists should be sent; and accordingly two thousand five hundred were transported thither
notes: Senate debate had included votes for demolishing Luceria instead; distance and hostile surroundings made citizens reluctant — enrollment friction echoing the Antium pattern (III.1).

quote: secret conspiracies were formed among the leading men at Capua, as well as at other places
notes: Heads of the conspiracy, the Calavii, die by suicide before formal charges — 'either through fear of the dictator's power, or the consciousness of guilt'.

quote: it was resolved that a dictator should be appointed to enforce these inquiries. Caius Maenius was accordingly nominated
notes: Dictatorship used as an investigative magistracy (quaestiones); inquiry then extended from Capua to electoral cabals at Rome itself, construing the senate's order broadly.

quote: they were most honourably acquitted of all the charges brought by the nobles
notes: Nobles under investigation counter-attacked the investigators; Maenius abdicated the dictatorship specifically to stand trial as a private citizen and was acquitted — Machiavelli discusses this episode in Disc. I.58/III context of calumnies vs accusations.

quote: being disagreeable to the nobility, was brought to trial, and acquitted
notes: Serial consul and reformer prosecuted amid the cabal inquiries and acquitted; Livy notes the inquiry then sank to lesser men and was finally suppressed by the very factions it targeted.

quote: until Caius Pœtelius, being nominated dictator, with Marcus Foslius, master of the horse, received the command of the army from the new consuls
notes: Variant tradition recorded by Livy: Poetelius was created merely to drive the nail (clavi figendi causa) on account of a pestilence — religious-emergency dictatorship.

quote: The colonies of Suessa and Pontiae were established in this year
notes: Same year: senate decree for Interamna and Cassinum, with 4,000 colonists sent by the next consuls — a cluster of strategic colonization.

quote: nominated Caius Junius Bubulcus dictator
notes: Etruscan war scare; the sick consul nominates by senate direction; dictator enforces a full levy of the younger citizens.

quote: on account of his having made the road, [called after him, the Appian,] and for having conveyed water into the city
notes: Appian Way and first aqueduct built by a censor acting alone; colleague Plautius abdicated in shame at the scandalous lectio senatus; Appius also transferred the Hercules cult from the Potitii to public slaves.

actors: consuls C. Junius Bubulcus and Q. Aemilius Barbula
quote: they declared, that they would pay no regard to such election, which had been made without distinction of right or wrong
notes: Consuls publicly nullify the Appian-Plautian senate roll and call the house in its pre-censorship order — inter-magistral conflict over control of senate composition; taxonomy fit imperfect (coded veto-deadlock as institutional blocking action).

quote: sixteen of the tribunes, for four legions, should be appointed by the people
notes: Plebiscite transfers appointment of 16 military tribunes from commanders to popular election — military patronage shifted to the comitia.

quote: the people likewise should constitute two naval commissioners, for the equipping and refitting of the fleet
notes: Creation of the duumviri navales by plebiscite — birth of a standing naval administration, popularly elected.

quote: The flute-players, taking offence because they had been prohibited by the last censors from holding their repasts in the temple of Jupiter
notes: A professional collegium's walkout to Tibur over withdrawn privileges, resolved by negotiation-plus-ruse and restoration of the privilege; coded as (guild) secession with low confidence — not class conflict, but a genuine labor-withdrawal bargaining event affecting state religion.

groups: tribunician college (6 for prosecution, 3 for Appius)
quote: he ordered the censor to be seized, and borne to prison
notes: Sempronius enforces the Aemilian 18-month limit against Appius's continued censorship; arrest ordered, but three tribunes interpose and Appius holds the censorship alone 'to the great disgust of all ranks' — ordinary channels invoked on both sides, outcome a legal stalemate; spans 9:33-34.

quote: five deputies, with two plebeian tribunes, had come hither, to charge Fabius, in the name of the senate, not to attempt to pass the Ciminian forest
notes: Senate attempts to restrain a consul's strategic initiative via deputies and tribunes; they arrive after the expedition has succeeded and 'rejoicing that they had arrived too late' report the victory — attempted institutional check mooted by events.

quote: in the silent time of the night, according to the established custom, he nominated Lucius Papirius dictator
notes: Fabius nominates his personal enemy at the senate's request, in total silence, refusing thanks — private enmity overridden by institutional form; first curiate vote postponed by the ill-omened Faucian curia (which had voted first in the years of the Gallic sack and Caudium).

quote: his election was stopped by a protest of Lucius Furius, plebeian tribune, until he resigned the censorship
notes: Per some annals (Livy flags the source), Appius stood for consul while still censor and was blocked by tribunician protest until resignation; as consul he then stayed in Rome 'to increase his interest by city intrigues' while Fabius's command was prorogued over his opposition.

quote: was granted the freedom of the state, without the right of voting
notes: Differential settlement: loyal Hernican states keep their own laws by preference, the defeated receive civitas sine suffragio with assemblies and intermarriage prohibited — citizenship wielded as a graded political instrument; equestrian statue voted to Marcius in the forum.

quote: By these the election of consuls was held, being the purpose for which they had been created
notes: Elections dictatorship because both consuls were tied to their armies; Livy notes Piso's annals omit two consular years here — documentary divergence flagged in the source.

quote: so much indignation did the election of Flavius excite, that most of the nobles laid aside their gold rings and bracelets
notes: A freedman's son elected curule aedile by the 'forum faction' built up under Appius's censorship; nobles respond with ostentatious mourning; Livy: 'From that time the state was split into two parties.'

quote: He made public the rules of proceeding in judicial causes, hitherto shut up in the closets of the pontiffs
notes: Publication of the legis actiones and the court calendar (dies fasti) — deprivatization of legal-procedural knowledge; triggered a counter-law requiring senate/tribune authorization for future temple dedications.

quote: purged the rest of the tribes of all the rabble of the forum, and threw it into four, and called them city tribes
notes: Electoral counter-reform confining the urban mass to four tribes, neutralizing the Flavian faction's comitial weight; earned Fabius the surname Maximus 'which he had not obtained by his many victories'; annual equestrian review (transvectio) also instituted.

quote: Colonies were led out to Sora and Alba. For the latter, situated in the country of the Aequans, six thousand colonists were enrolled.
notes: Six thousand colonists to Alba, four thousand to Sora, both on recently hostile frontiers.

quote: the heads of that conspiracy, after a trial before the consuls, held in pursuance of a decree of the senate, were beaten with rods and beheaded
notes: Frusinates fined a third of their lands for tampering with the Hernici; leaders tried and executed under senatorial decree.

quote: to quell this insurrection, Caius Junius Bubulcus was nominated dictator
notes: Dictator against the Aequan rising; triumphed and dedicated the temple of Health on the eighth day.

quote: Marcus Valerius Maximus was nominated dictator, and chose for his master of the horse Marcus Aemilius Paullus
notes: Dictator against Etruscan rebellion and Marsian seizure of the Carseoli colony lands; a variant in 10:5 has him pacifying Arretium by composing the Cilnian dissensions without battle.

quote: Marcus Valerius was elected consul, before the expiration of his dictatorship, many have believed, without his soliciting the office
notes: Irregular but consensual: sitting dictator elected consul in absentia by an interrex; Livy reports it as tradition (many have believed).

groups: plebeians of consular and triumphal rank
quote: the four additional pontiffs and five augurs should all be chosen out of the commons
notes: Ogulnian law opening pontificates and augurates to plebeians; debate Appius vs Decius spans 10:6-10:8; passed in 10:9 after a one-day tribunician protest, first plebeian pontiffs and augurs named.

quote: Marcus Valerius, consul, procured a law to be passed concerning appeals; more carefully enforced by additional sanctions
notes: Third enactment of the lex Valeria de provocatione, always by the same family; Livy explains the renewals by the overbearing influence of the few against the liberty of the commons.

quote: and two tribes were added, the Aniensian and Terentine
notes: Censors complete the survey and enlarge the tribal structure to accommodate new citizen territory.

quote: A colony was sent thither as a barrier against the Umbrians, and called Narnia, from the river Nar
notes: Strategic colony at captured Nequinum; explicitly a military barrier rather than a land-hunger measure.

quote: The dearness of provisions also distressed the state very much, and they would have felt the extremity of want
notes: Scarcity managed administratively: Fabius as curule aedile regulates the market and forms grain magazines (per the tradition Livy cites).

quote: An interregnum took place this year, the reason of which is not mentioned
notes: Constitutional gap of unstated cause; two interreges before Sulpicius holds the consular election.

quote: This year a colony was carried out to Carseoli
notes: Four thousand colonists per 10:3; planted in Aequicolan territory.

quote: he ordered that clause to be read aloud by which it was not lawful that the same person shall be re-elected consul within ten years
notes: Fabius invokes the ten-year iteration ban against his own re-election; tribunes offer statutory exemption; the centuries elect him anyway and he negotiates Decius as colleague — legality bent through ordinary channels.

quote: great numbers were prosecuted by the aediles, for having in possession larger quantities of land than the state allowed
notes: Enforcement of a statutory landholding cap by aedilician prosecution with near-universal conviction — direct evidence that a holding limit existed and was litigable in 298 BCE; key datum for the Disc I.37 land-tenure-register hypothesis.

quote: besought him to raise up the consulship out of the plebeian mire, and to restore both to the office itself, and to the patrician rank, their original dignity
notes: Patrician attempt to recover both consulships; Fabius refuses the illegal double-patrician return; Appius elected with the plebeian Volumnius instead.

quote: a sedition having been raised among the Lucanians by the plebeians and the more indigent of the people
notes: Class-based sedition in an allied state, suppressed by a Roman proconsular army to the satisfaction of the Lucanian nobles — not a Roman domestic event, included as Rome-managed allied unrest.

quote: the senate ordered the courts of justice to be shut, and a levy to be made of men of every description
notes: Emergency justitium with extraordinary enlistment categories (elder cohorts, freedmen's sons incorporated in the centuries) under the four-nation coalition scare; coded new-institution for the enlistment innovation.

quote: But persons were not readily found to give in their names; because they considered that they were being sent into what was almost a perpetual advanced guard in a hostile country
notes: Colonies decreed for Minturnae and Sinuessa; enrollment shortfall because sites were seen as garrison duty, not land provision — parallel to the Antium under-enrollment used in Disc I.37.

quote: This altar I dedicate to plebeian chastity, and exhort you
notes: Status conflict in the religious sphere: patrician matrons exclude a patrician woman married to a plebeian consul; she founds a parallel plebeian cult — institutional duplication as conflict resolution.

quote: the Ogulnii, Cneius and Quintus, being curule aediles, carried on prosecutions against several usurers
notes: Debt-law enforcement by fines, proceeds converted to public monuments; plebeian aediles the same year fined farmers of the public pastures — twin enforcement actions against economic offenses.

quote: the patricians endeavouring that Fabius should have Etruria for his province, without casting lots
notes: Inter-order fight over command assignment (senate allocation vs sortition); argued before the people and settled by popular decree for Fabius — Livy frames it as order-conflict more than personal rivalry.

quote: Quintus Fabius Gurges, the consul's son, having prosecuted some matrons before the people on a charge of adultery
notes: Morals prosecutions before the people amid pestilence and prodigies; fines fund the temple of Venus near the circus.

quote: by the support of three plebeian tribunes, in opposition to the protest of the other seven, and the declared judgment of the senate, he triumphed
notes: Consul triumphs against senatorial judgment and a 7-tribune protest, claiming popular will suffices; cites precedents of people-authorized triumphs — a constitutional collision resolved by raw assertion within split institutions.

quote: The ill humour in the commons was further exasperated, because the tax for the payment of the army was collected by contribution
notes: Fiscal grievance, not riot: Papirius banks all silver and brass in the treasury while the army-pay tax is still levied; contrast with Carvilius's donative the same year. Coded riot-tumult for lack of a grievance type; no violence.

quote: evaded, as was said, the jurisdiction of the people, by procuring the commission of lieutenant-general
notes: Tribunician prosecution of the ex-consul aborted when the consul's favor gives him a legateship shielding him from popular jurisdiction — an accusation channel blocked by office-holding.

quote: in consequence of some irregularity in their appointments, others had been, within five days after, substituted in their room
notes: Defective tribunician election corrected by prompt substitution.

quote: And some, decreeing Spain and Africa as provinces for the consuls, thought the war should be maintained both by sea and land
notes: Senate splits three ways over provinces and war strategy after the Saguntine appeal, adopting the cautious course of sending envoys first; coded as command-assignment dispute for lack of a dedicated war-debate type.

quote: It was then proposed to the people, whether they willed and commanded that war should be declared against the people of Carthage
notes: Formal war vote by the people with province sortition, six legions decreed and a city-wide supplication (21:16-17), war then declared at Carthage by Fabius's embassy (21:18); nearest v1 type for a formal state decision.

quote: the colonies of Placentia and Cremona had been lately planted in the Gallic territory about the Po
notes: Recent foundation of the Latin colonies Placentia and Cremona with triumvirs assigning lands, reported retrospectively as the grievance behind the Boii rising.

quote: even the Roman triumvirs, Caius Lutatius, Caius Servilius, and Titus Annius, who had come to assign the lands, distrusting the walls of Placentia, fled to Mutina
notes: Boii revolt against the new colonies drives out the land-assignment triumvirs and treacherously seizes Roman envoys at a parley, remaining unresolved as Manlius's relief column is ambushed; borderline domestic since the rebels are Gallic subjects.

quote: they order Caius Atilius, the praetor, to carry assistance to Manlius with one Roman legion and five thousand of the allies
notes: Senate's emergency reinforcement decree for the Gallic rising and the levy of a replacement legion for the consul Scipio; routine mobilization coded under the nearest formal-decision type.

quote: Two thousand infantry and two hundred horse, having killed the guards at the gates, desert to Hannibal
notes: Gallic auxiliaries in Scipio's camp massacre the gate guards by night and defect to Hannibal, prompting the consul to shift camp to the Trebia.

quote: Dasius, a Brundusian, the governor of the garrison, having been corrupted for four hundred pieces of gold
notes: The Italian commander of the Roman grain magazine at Clastidium is bribed and surrenders the post to Hannibal, who uses it as a granary.

quote: The approaching period of the elections also stimulated him, lest the war should be protracted till the new consuls were chosen
notes: Command dispute between the consuls over giving battle (21:52-53), Sempronius overriding his wounded colleague partly to secure glory before the elections, which led directly to the Trebia defeat.

quote: Such terror on account of this disaster was carried to Rome, that they believed that the enemy was already approaching the city with hostile standards
notes: Panic grips Rome after Trebia and Sempronius runs the enemy's lines to hold the consular elections, at which Servilius and Flaminius are returned; collective alarm without violence, hence low-grade tumult.

quote: On account of the other prodigies the decemvirs were ordered to consult the books
notes: Winter prodigies at Rome are expiated by decree with Sibylline consultation, a nine-day festival, lectisternia, dedications and new decennial vows by the praetor Atilius Serranus.

quote: He had a design to enter on the consulship in his province, recollecting his old contests with the fathers
notes: Consul-elect Flaminius slips out of Rome to enter office at Ariminum, evading auspices and the Latin festival, and defies the senate's embassy of recall amid an ill-omened inaugural sacrifice.

quote: that no senator, or he who had been father of a senator, should possess a ship fit for sea service
notes: Retrospective notice of the tribune Q. Claudius's plebiscite barring senators from owning sea-going ships, carried against fierce senatorial opposition with Flaminius its lone senatorial backer; anchored at 21:63.

quote: They said that they had created indeed two consuls, that they had but one
notes: Senate indignation at Flaminius entering his consulship without taking the auspices, a dispute over the legitimacy of his magistracy (livy:en:22:1).

quote: Proclamation was made through the city, that the Saturnalia should be kept for a day and a night
notes: After mass prodigies the senate decreed expiations, a lectisternium, and perpetual observance of the Saturnalia as a holiday (livy:en:22:1).

quote: On the first intelligence of this defeat at Rome, a concourse of the people, dismayed and terrified, took place in the forum
notes: News of Trasimene produced a terrified concourse in the forum, calmed only by the praetor's announcement while senators deliberated for days (livy:en:22:7).

quote: the people created Quintus Fabius Maximus pro-dictator, and Marcus Minucius Rufus master of the horse
notes: With the surviving consul absent, the people unprecedentedly created Fabius pro-dictator and Minucius master of the horse (livy:en:22:8; cf. 22:31).

quote: first of all, the people should be consulted respecting a sacred spring: that it could not be without the order of the people
notes: On the pontifex maximus's ruling a sacred spring (ver sacrum) was vowed by formal order of the people, with great games and new temples (livy:en:22:10).

quote: sons of freedmen even, who had children, and were of the military age, had taken the oath
notes: The emergency levy at Rome extended enrollment even to sons of freedmen, an irregular widening of military obligation (livy:en:22:11).

quote: they showed evidently that they would have preferred Minucius to Fabius for their general
notes: Minucius's harangue against Fabian delay drew tribunes, knights and common soldiers into open insubordinate preference for the master of the horse (livy:en:22:14).

quote: he sent his son Quintus to Rome and sold his farm, uninjured by the enemy, and thus redeemed the public credit at his own private expense
notes: Coded as closest type: the senate withheld silver for Fabius's prisoner exchange because he had not consulted the fathers, so he sold his farm to redeem the public credit (livy:en:22:23).

quote: he would bring forward a moderate proposition, to make the authority of the master of the horse and the dictator equal
notes: Tribune Metilius attacked the dictator and carried, with Varro's sole senatorial support, the unprecedented bill equalizing Minucius's command with Fabius's (livy:en:22:25; passage noted 22:26).

quote: nor would he divide the command with him with respect to times or days, but that he would divide the army
notes: Fabius refused alternate-day exercise of the equalized command and instead divided the legions and camps with Minucius, consul-fashion (livy:en:22:27).

quote: That order of the people, therefore, with which I have been oppressed rather than honoured, I first cancel and annul
notes: After his rescue Minucius voluntarily cancelled the people's equalization decree and returned himself and his legions to the dictator's authority and auspices (livy:en:22:30).

quote: twenty-five slaves were crucified for forming a conspiracy in the Campus Martius; his liberty was given to the informer
notes: A slave conspiracy in the Campus Martius was suppressed by crucifixion of twenty-five slaves, with freedom and cash for the informer; a Carthaginian spy was also mutilated (livy:en:22:33).

quote: Lucius Veturius Philo was nominated, who chose Manius Pomponius Matho master of the horse
notes: A dictator was named to hold the consular elections but, created with an auspicial defect, was forced to abdicate on the fourteenth day, and the state fell to an interregnum (livy:en:22:33).

quote: During the interregnum of the latter the election was held, with a violent contest between the patricians and the people
notes: The consular election under the interrex became a violent class contest, tribune Herennius charging the nobility with inviting and prolonging the war to block a truly plebeian consul (livy:en:22:34).

quote: Terentius alone was created consul, that the comitia for choosing his colleague might be in his own management
notes: Varro was returned alone against the patrician candidates, and the nobles pressed the reluctant Aemilius Paulus on him as a counterweight rather than a colleague (livy:en:22:35).

quote: the soldiers were bound by an oath, which had never before been the case, dictated by the military tribunes
notes: For the first time the soldiers' voluntary compact not to desert their ranks was converted into a legally compulsory oath dictated by the military tribunes (livy:en:22:38).

quote: when he could no longer withstand the sedition and the leader of the sedition, he sends Marius Statilius, a prefect
notes: Soldiers clamoured to plunder Hannibal's seemingly deserted camp and threatened to advance without their leaders until escaped slaves exposed the ambush, restoring the consuls' authority (livy:en:22:42).

quote: Varro, on the following day, on which it was his turn to hold the command, without consulting his colleague, displayed the signal for battle
notes: Coded as closest type for the consular command deadlock: under alternate-day command Varro gave the battle signal at Cannae without consulting Paulus, who followed under protest (livy:en:22:45).

quote: certain noble youths, the chief of whom was Lucius Caecilius Metellus, turned their attention to the sea and ships
notes: At Canusium young Scipio broke up at sword-point the plot of Metellus's noble youths to abandon Italy, forcing them to swear loyalty and surrendering them to custody (livy:en:22:53).

quote: to keep the women from coming into public, and compel each to abide within her own threshold; to put a stop to the lamentations of families
notes: Amid unprecedented panic after Cannae (22:54) the senate adopted Fabius's emergency measures: confining women, silencing lamentation, posting gate guards and controlling news (livy:en:22:55).

quote: the mourning was limited to thirty days, by a decree of the senate
notes: With every matron in mourning the rites of Ceres were intermitted, and the senate decreed a thirty-day limit on mourning so other sacred rites could proceed (livy:en:22:56).

quote: two vestal virgins, Opimia and Floronia, were that year convicted of incontinence
notes: The Vestals Opimia and Floronia were convicted of unchastity, one buried alive at the Colline gate, while the pontiff's secretary Cantilius was scourged to death (livy:en:22:57).

quote: a Gallic man and woman, and a Greek man and woman, were let down alive in the cattle market
notes: Extraordinary expiations from the books of fate included the live burial of Gallic and Greek couples, a rite by no means Roman, and Fabius Pictor was sent to consult Delphi (livy:en:22:57).

quote: Marcus Junius, created dictator on the authority of the senate, and Titus Sempronius, master of the horse, proclaiming a levy
notes: Marcus Junius was created dictator on the senate's authority to hold the emergency levy, enrolling youths from seventeen and even boys still wearing the praetexta (livy:en:22:57).

quote: they armed eight thousand stout youths from the slaves, purchased at the public expense, first inquiring of each whether he was willing to serve
notes: From scarcity of free men a new form of levy armed eight thousand slave volunteers bought at public expense, preferred even to ransoming the captives (livy:en:22:57).

quote: With these was sent Carthalo, a noble Carthaginian, who might propose terms, if perchance their minds were inclined towards peace
notes: Hannibal's envoy Carthalo, sent with the captives' delegates to sound out peace, was ordered by the dictator's lictor to leave Roman territory before nightfall (livy:en:22:58).

quote: The sad reply, that the captives would not be ransomed, being delivered
notes: After Torquatus's indictment of the captives' cowardice (22:60) the senate refused to ransom the Cannae prisoners, and the delegate who evaded his oath was surrendered to Hannibal (livy:en:22:61).

quote: The people who revolted to the Carthaginians were these: the Atellani, Calatini, the Hirpini, some of the Apulians
notes: After Cannae Italian allies began revolting to Carthage in despair of the empire, though the Romans made no mention of peace (livy:en:22:61).

quote: was met in crowds of all ranks of citizens, and thanks bestowed because he had not despaired of the republic
notes: Coded as the pointed inverse of a prosecution: the returning Varro, chief author of the defeat, was met by crowds and thanked for not despairing of the republic (livy:en:22:61).

quote: the Mopsian party had retired from the city; which was thus given up to the Carthaginian without opposition
notes: Factional struggle at Compsa (livy:en:23:1): pro-Carthaginian Trebius ousts the pro-Roman Mopsii faction and hands the town to Hannibal.

quote: he adopted a plan by which he might preserve the senate and render it subject to himself and the commons
notes: At Capua (livy:en:23:2) Pacuvius Calavius locks the senators in the senate-house, posing as accomplice of a popular plot, to make the senate dependent on him; episode famously retold by Machiavelli.

quote: I will give you the opportunity of pronouncing upon the life or death of each
notes: Staged popular judgment on each Capuan senator (livy:en:23:3); unable to name better replacements, the assembly releases the senate, completing Pacuvius's trick.

quote: Pacuvius, having thus rendered the senators more subservient to himself than to the commons by the gift of their lives, ruled without the aid of arms
notes: Outcome of the trick (livy:en:23:4): Pacuvius dominates Capua, the senate flatters the commons, and respect for law and Rome collapses.

quote: with difficulty obtained that ambassadors should be sent to the Roman consul
notes: Relatives of the 300 Campanian horsemen in Sicily push Capua to send envoys to the consul at Venusia (livy:en:23:5), whose despairing speech discredits the Roman cause.

quote: Immediately the commons and the major part of the senate turned their attention to revolt
notes: After Vibius Virius's report (livy:en:23:6), Capuan commons and senate majority resolve on defection and send the same ambassadors on to Hannibal over elder resistance.

quote: requiring that one of the consuls should be elected from Campania if they wished assistance
notes: Variant tradition Livy declines to vouch for (livy:en:23:6): Campanian envoys demand a Campanian consul and are expelled from the senate-house by a lictor.

quote: The ambassadors came to Hannibal and concluded a treaty of peace with him
notes: Capua defects from the Roman alliance (livy:en:23:7) on terms preserving its own laws and magistrates and exempting Campanians from Carthaginian command.

quote: be shut up in the baths, as if for the purpose of keeping them in custody; where, suffocated with heat and vapour, they might expire in a horrid manner
notes: On the commons' order (livy:en:23:7) Roman prefects and citizens at Capua are seized and suffocated in the baths as the revolt is consummated.

quote: Forthwith will I ratify the alliance with Rome with the blood of Hannibal
notes: Perolla, son of Pacuvius, plans to assassinate Hannibal at the banquet (livy:en:23:8) but is privately dissuaded by his father (23:9) and throws the sword away.

quote: ordered Decius Magius to be apprehended, and to be placed by himself before his feet to plead his cause
notes: Hannibal demands the loyalist Decius Magius, resister of the defection since 23:7; the Capuan senate acquiesces and he is arrested, haranguing the crowd, and deported (livy:en:23:10).

quote: Quintus Fabius Pictor, the ambassador, returned from Delphi to Rome, and read the response of the oracle
notes: Fabius Pictor reports the Delphic oracle's prescriptions after Cannae and the senate decrees the enjoined supplications (livy:en:23:11).

quote: those who would serve as soldiers with him, he would order to be released from their liability to punishment and their debts
notes: Dictator M. Junius Pera's last-resort levy (livy:en:23:14): 6,000 capital convicts and judgment debtors enrolled and armed with captured Gallic spoils.

quote: the commons, as usual, were all inclined to a change in the government and to espouse the cause of Hannibal
notes: Nolan senate, pro-Roman against pro-Hannibal commons, feigns consent to revolt while secretly summoning the praetor Marcellus (livy:en:23:14).

quote: he had conceived a wish to put Nola under the power and dominion of the Carthaginian
notes: Lucius Bantius contemplates betraying Nola out of gratitude to Hannibal; Marcellus co-opts him with praise, a horse, and money rather than punishment (livy:en:23:15).

quote: conferences were held by night between the commons of Nola and the Carthaginians
notes: Nolan commons plot to plunder Roman baggage and shut the gates for Hannibal; senate informs Marcellus, who forestalls it by battle (livy:en:23:16).

quote: He beheaded more than seventy who were convicted of treason, and ordered their goods to be confiscated to the Roman state
notes: Marcellus's judicial inquiry at Nola (livy:en:23:17) into collusion with Hannibal; 70+ executed, goods confiscated, government handed back to the senate.

quote: they endeavoured to chew the thongs and skins which they tore from their shields
notes: Siege famine at Casilinum (livy:en:23:19): Gracchus floats grain casks down the Vulturnus; garrison finally ransomed at seven ounces of gold per head.

quote: The Petelini, unable to bear up against these distresses, sent ambassadors to Rome to solicit aid
notes: Petelia (loyal Bruttian polity) appeals to the Roman senate, which confesses it cannot protect distant allies; the Petelian senate debates flight, defection, or defense and resolves to fortify (livy:en:23:20).

quote: on the proposal of Marcus Minucius, plebeian tribune, a financial triumvirate was appointed
notes: Amid acute scarcity of money a board of triumviri mensarii is created by tribunician proposal (livy:en:23:21).

quote: having sent ambassadors to Hiero, the only source of assistance the Romans had, received as much money as was wanting to pay the troops
notes: With Rome unable to supply pay or corn for Sicily, Otacilius appeals to King Hiero, who funds pay and six months' grain (livy:en:23:21).

quote: the freedom of the state should be conferred upon two senators from each of the Latin states
notes: Carvilius's proposal to recruit Latin senators is shouted down and buried in silence at Fabius Maximus's urging (livy:en:23:22); coded as conflict over access to office.

quote: nominated Marcus Fabius Buteo dictator, for six months, without a master of the horse
notes: To replenish the senate depleted since Cannae, Varro is recalled and names M. Fabius Buteo dictator without a master of the horse, an unprecedented arrangement (livy:en:23:22).

quote: Having thus elected one hundred and seventy-seven senators, with the entire approbation of his countrymen, he instantly abdicated his office
notes: Buteo protests the irregularity of his own office, revises the roll by fixed criteria of rank and valor, enrolls 177 senators, and abdicates at once (livy:en:23:23).

quote: the shops were shut up as if the solitude of night reigned through the city
notes: Public panic in Rome after Postumius's army is annihilated in Gaul; the senate orders the aediles to reopen shops and end the display of mourning (livy:en:23:25); coded low as tumult without violence.

quote: The people ordered that Marcus Marcellus should be in command as proconsul, because he was the only Roman general who had been successful
notes: Command prorogation by popular vote (livy:en:23:30): proconsular imperium conferred on Marcellus for his successes at Nola.

quote: double taxes should be imposed for that year, one moiety of which should be immediately levied
notes: Emergency war finance (livy:en:23:31): senate decrees doubled tribute, half collected at once to pay all troops except the Cannae survivors.

quote: the gods were displeased, because on that occasion, for the first time, two plebeians had been elected consuls
notes: Marcellus's consular election is annulled on augural grounds amid patrician claims against two plebeian consuls; he abdicates and Fabius Maximus is elected (livy:en:23:31).

quote: to make Roman citizens of the three hundred Campanian horsemen who had returned to Rome after having faithfully served
notes: Citizenship grant resolving the status of the loyal 300 Campanian horsemen (livy:en:23:31), retroactively deemed citizens of Cumae from the day before Capua's revolt.

quote: when that plan did not succeed, they contrived an artifice by which to entrap them
notes: Capuan plot to seize Cumae at the Hamae sacrifice after failed solicitation to revolt; Cumae alerts Gracchus, who storms the Campanian camp killing the medix tuticus Marius Alfius (livy:en:23:35).

quote: deliberations were held clandestinely on the subject of massacring the nobles and betraying the city
notes: Second year of Nolan sedition (livy:en:23:39): commons again plot to kill the nobles and hand the city to Hannibal; Fabius interposes his army and sends Marcellus to garrison Nola.

quote: Ambassadors were therefore despatched from both nations at the same time to Hannibal
notes: Hirpini and Caudine Samnites, Italian allies of Carthage, protest to Hannibal that they are left defenseless against Marcellus's raids; he rebuffs them with promises and presents (livy:en:23:42-43).

quote: had they intended to surrender themselves to Hannibal, they should not have called a Roman garrison to their aid
notes: Hanno's solicitation of Nola's defection (livy:en:23:43) is formally refused by the senator Herennius Bassus (livy:en:23:44); coded as defection politics of an Italian polity, appeal direction inverted.

quote: one thousand two hundred and seventy-two horsemen, Numidians and Spaniards, deserted to Marcellus
notes: Mass desertion from Hannibal's army after the defeat at Nola (livy:en:23:46), attributed to pique or hope of better service; army politics on the Carthaginian side, hence low confidence.

quote: they entered into the contract, and the affairs of the state were conducted by private funds
notes: Following Fulvius's appeal to the revenue-farmers (livy:en:23:48), three companies of nineteen contract to supply Spain on credit, with exemption from military service and state insurance of shipping losses (livy:en:23:49).

quote: the city was surrendered to the Carthaginians, with an appearance of perfect unanimity
notes: A Locrian popular assembly, under coercion and led by its fickler elements, votes to abandon Rome and surrender the city to Carthage (livy:en:24:1).

quote: the commons dissented from the nobles; the senate favouring the Romans, while the commons endeavoured to draw the states over to the Carthaginians
notes: Class strife at Croto: the commons under Aristomachus admit the Bruttians into the city while the nobles hold the citadel and are later evacuated to Locri (livy:en:24:2; sequel in 24:3).

quote: by voluntarily resigning the guardianship which he shared with several others, united the powers of all in himself
notes: On Hiero's death at Syracuse the boy Hieronymus succeeds and Andranodorus ousts the other fourteen guardians to concentrate power in himself (livy:en:24:4).

quote: It was at this time that a conspiracy formed against the life of the tyrant was discovered by a certain servant
notes: A conspiracy against the tyrant Hieronymus of Syracuse is betrayed by a servant; Theodotus under torture shields his accomplices by accusing the innocent (livy:en:24:5).

quote: The naming of Thraso gave the highest degree of credibility to the story in the mind of the tyrant. Accordingly he was immediately given up to punishment
notes: Thraso, the sole pro-Roman voice at Hieronymus's court, is falsely accused and executed, severing the bond holding the Roman alliance (livy:en:24:5).

quote: Hieronymus sent ambassadors to Carthage, to conclude a league in conformity with the alliance with Hannibal
notes: Hieronymus insults Rome's envoys and concludes a league with Carthage, demanding first half and then all of Sicily (livy:en:24:6).

quote: an attack being made upon the king, as he passed by unattended by his guards, he was pierced with several wounds before any assistance could be brought
notes: The conspirators ambush and assassinate the tyrant Hieronymus in a narrow street at Leontini, Dinomenes delaying the guards (livy:en:24:7); the regime-change struggle follows in 24:21-32.

quote: The prerogative century proceeded to vote a second time, when Quintus Fabius Maximus for the fourth time, and Marcus Marcellus for the third time, were created consuls
notes: Presiding consul Fabius halts the consular vote, lectures the centuries, silences the protesting Otacilius with a reminder of the axes in the fasces, and is himself re-elected (speech in livy:en:24:8; quote and outcome at livy:en:24:9).

quote: Then first it happened that the Roman fleet was manned at the expense of individuals
notes: Facing an empty treasury and war in Sicily, a senate decree obliges citizens by property class to furnish and pay sailors, the first privately funded manning of the fleet (livy:en:24:11).

quote: The commons of Nola, who had been long disaffected to the Romans and at enmity with their own senate
notes: The commons of Nola, at odds with their own senate, send envoys promising to surrender the city to Hannibal, but Marcellus forestalls them by garrisoning the town (livy:en:24:13).

quote: that the commons were under the influence of the youth, and the state of Tarentum in the hands of the commons
notes: Five noble Tarentine youths plot with Hannibal to betray Tarentum, claiming the commons who control the state will deliver the city (livy:en:24:13); the attempt fails at 24:20.

quote: I bid you, said he, all be free, and may the event be attended with advantage, happiness, and prosperity to the state and to yourselves
notes: After the volones murmured for their promised freedom (livy:en:24:14) and won the battle of Beneventum, Gracchus, authorized by the senate, manumits the slave legions en masse (quote at livy:en:24:16).

quote: through fear of punishment, took possession of a hill not far from the camp
notes: About four thousand volones who had fought half-heartedly withdraw to a hill fearing punishment; Gracchus frees them too but stigmatizes the seceders with a penalty of eating standing (livy:en:24:16).

quote: they pronounced them guilty of having used words and discourse prejudicial to the state, that a conspiracy might be formed for the abandonment of Italy
notes: The censors degrade and disfranchise Metellus and those who plotted after Cannae to abandon Italy, oath-evading prisoners, and over two thousand draft-shirkers, whom the senate ships to Sicily (livy:en:24:18).

quote: the property of minors first, and then the portions of widows, began to be brought in
notes: With the treasury empty, contractors work on credit, owners defer payment for freed volones, private trusts are deposited with the state, and officers refuse pay (livy:en:24:18).

quote: calling the people at once to liberty and arms, bid them assemble in the Achradina
notes: After the tyrannicide the conspirators rouse Syracuse to liberty; Andranodorus seizes the Island but submits (livy:en:24:22), and praetors including Andranodorus are elected while royal treasure passes to quaestors (livy:en:24:23); quote at livy:en:24:21.

quote: slew Themistus and Andranodorus as soon as they had entered the senate-house
notes: Urged by his royal wife, Andranodorus plots with Themistus to seize power; the actor Ariston informs, and the praetors with senate sanction kill both in the senate-house (livy:en:24:24).

quote: a decree, which was consented to almost before it was proposed, that all the royal family should be put to death
notes: After Sopater's speech the assembly decrees death to the whole royal house, and Demarata and Harmonia are immediately killed (livy:en:24:25).

quote: they dragged her from the sanctuary and murdered her; and after that they fell upon the virgins
notes: Heraclea and her virgin daughters are butchered at the household altar just before a countermanding reprieve arrives, turning popular feeling to anger and a demand for new elections (livy:en:24:26).

quote: one person from the extremity of the crowd nominated Epicydes, and then another from the same quarter nominated Hippocrates
notes: A packed assembly of commons, soldiers, and deserters forces the intimidated praetors to declare Hannibal's agents Hippocrates and Epicydes praetors of Syracuse (livy:en:24:27).

quote: it was resolved that a treaty of peace should be formed, and that ambassadors should be sent with those from Rome to ratify the same
notes: With insurrection imminent between pro-Roman and pro-Carthaginian factions, Apollonides's speech sways the assembly and council to renew the Roman alliance (livy:en:24:28).

quote: the praetors, in the utmost consternation, rode away to Syracuse during the confusion. The mutiny, however, was not quelled even by their flight
notes: Sheltered by the Cretans, Hippocrates inflames the army with a forged letter from the praetors to Marcellus; the troops mutiny and attack the Syracusan soldiers (livy:en:24:30-31; quote at livy:en:24:31).

quote: the slaves were invited to liberty, and those bound in prison were released; after which this mixed rabble created Hippocrates and Epicydes their praetors
notes: The army forces the Hexapylum gates, the Achradina falls, the praetors are massacred, and Syracuse relapses into servitude under Hippocrates and Epicydes (livy:en:24:32).

quote: The people of Enna thus shut up in the pit were put to the sword
notes: After Enna's leading men demand the keys and their liberty in assembly (livy:en:24:37), the Roman prefect Pinarius has his garrison massacre the assembled citizens in the theatre, a deed Marcellus does not disapprove (quote at livy:en:24:39).

quote: Lucius Metellus, a plebeian tribune, immediately appointed a day for impleading the censors, Publius Furius and Marcus Atilius, before the people
notes: Tribune Metellus, disfranchised for the Cannae conspiracy, prosecutes the censors before the people, but the other nine tribunes shield them from answering in office (livy:en:24:43).

quote: The consuls elected were Quintus Fabius Maximus, son of the consul, and Tiberius Sempronius Gracchus a second time, both being absent
notes: Fabius presides over elections returning his own son and Gracchus, both absent, prolonging wartime continuity of command; coded low as Livy reports no overt contest (livy:en:24:43).

quote: some were of opinion that he ought to be scourged and put to death as a deserter
notes: The Roman council debates executing the double-traitor Dasius Altinius of Arpi; the elder Fabius's middle course of custody at Cales prevails, while Hannibal burns Altinius's family alive (livy:en:24:45).

quote: the senate commissioned Marcus Atilius, the city praetor, to rid the people of these superstitions
notes: Crowds practising foreign rites in the forum nearly assaulted the aediles who tried to clear them, so the senate ordered the city praetor to confiscate prophetic books and ban foreign rites (livy:en:25:1).

quote: Tiberius Sempronius, the consul, nominated Caius Claudius Centho as dictator to hold the election
notes: With both consuls kept at the war, a dictator was named solely to hold the consular elections, at which his own master of horse Fulvius Flaccus was returned consul (livy:en:25:2).

quote: the tribunes of the people opposed his pretensions to the aedileship
notes: Tribunes objected that the under-age Scipio could not stand for curule aedile, but popular enthusiasm at the vote made them abandon the challenge (livy:en:25:2).

quote: accused some matrons of misconduct before the people, and some of them they convicted and sent into exile
notes: The plebeian aediles prosecuted matrons for misconduct before the people, securing convictions and exile for some (livy:en:25:2).

quote: proposed that a fine of two hundred thousand asses should be imposed on Marcus Posthumius
notes: After the publican Postumius faked shipwrecks to defraud the state's shipping insurance, two tribunes brought him before the people for a 200,000-as fine, a prosecution that also impeded the consuls' levy (livy:en:25:3).

quote: the farmers of the revenue, forming themselves into a wedge, rushed into the void space occasioned by the removal of the people
notes: When the tribune Casca refused to veto the vote, the publicans charged the assembly on the Capitol and broke it up, the consul warning the tribunes to dismiss the commons before insurrection (livy:en:25:3).

quote: he would be adjudged an exile, his goods would be sold, and himself interdicted from water and fire
notes: After a senate decree branding the publicans' violence as prejudicial to the state, the tribunes converted the fine into a capital charge; Postumius fled into exile and the riot's ringleaders were imprisoned or exiled (livy:en:25:4).

quote: The election was contested with the greatest obstinacy by three candidates
notes: In a bitterly contested election for chief pontiff, the young Licinius Crassus defeated two senior ex-censors, a result without precedent for a hundred and twenty years (livy:en:25:5).

quote: ordered two triumvirates to be appointed, one of which within, the other without the fiftieth mile from the city
notes: Facing a scarcity of military-age men, the senate created two triumviral boards to enrol free-born boys under seventeen throughout the countryside (livy:en:25:5).

quote: the senate saw no reason why the interests of the republic should be intrusted to the hands of soldiers who had deserted their comrades
notes: The disgraced Cannae survivors petitioned Marcellus for restoration to active service, but the senate refused rehabilitation, leaving them to serve without rewards or return to Italy (speech livy:en:25:6, decision anchored livy:en:25:7).

quote: after being scourged with rods, with the approbation of the people, were thrown down from the rock
notes: The Tarentine hostages who escaped with Phileas were recaptured at Tarracina, scourged in the Comitium and hurled from the Tarpeian rock, a severity that drove Tarentum and Thurii toward revolt (livy:en:25:7).

quote: about thirteen noble Tarentine youths formed a conspiracy, the chief of whom were Nico and Philemenus
notes: Enraged by the execution of the hostages, thirteen young Tarentine nobles conspired with Hannibal to betray their city, negotiating that Tarentum keep its liberty and laws (livy:en:25:8).

quote: Hannibal gave orders to assemble the Tarentines without their arms
notes: After the conspirators opened the gates and the Roman garrison was driven into the citadel, Hannibal assembled the Tarentines, promised them autonomy, and had Roman houses marked and plundered (livy:en:25:10; entry narrated livy:en:25:9).

quote: This is the origin of the Apollinarian games, which were vowed and celebrated in order to victory
notes: The prophetic verses of Marcius, vindicated by their Cannae prediction, moved the senate and decemvirs to vow annual games to Apollo with mixed public and private funding, instituting the ludi Apollinares (livy:en:25:12).

quote: the Campanians were experiencing famine, that calamity which is the usual attendant of a protracted siege
notes: Famine inside blockaded Capua, caused by the Romans preventing sowing, drove the Campanians to beg Hannibal for grain convoys, which Hanno organized from Beneventum until Fulvius stormed his camp (livy:en:25:13).

quote: This plan of the general was disconcerted, after the signal began to sound for a retreat, by the clamours of the soldiery
notes: At Hanno's camp the troops shouted down the consul's retreat signal and stormed the rampart on their own initiative, forcing Fulvius to convert insubordination into an assault he then rewarded (livy:en:25:14).

groups: friends and relations of the hostages
quote: The friends and relations of these hostages sent a letter and a message to Hanno and Mago
notes: Kinsmen of the executed hostages at Thurii plotted with Hanno and Mago, shut the routed Romans out of the gates, and after internal division the city received the Carthaginians, Metapontum having likewise revolted (livy:en:25:15).

quote: unless he ratified his league with the enemy with the head and blood of the general, betrayed to them, though his guest
notes: Flavius, praetor of the pro-Roman Lucanian faction, switched sides and sealed his new Carthaginian alliance by luring his guest-friend the proconsul Gracchus into Mago's ambush, where he was killed (livy:en:25:16; variant accounts livy:en:25:17).

quote: he requested of the fathers that five thousand men might be placed at his disposal
notes: The senate irregularly entrusted eight thousand men to the centurion Centenius Penula on his own petition, a command assignment Livy derides and which Hannibal annihilated in Lucania (livy:en:25:19).

quote: as if discharged from service by the death of their general, left their standards
notes: Gracchus's army of volunteer slaves deserted en masse after his death, and the senate later ordered a search through the market towns to force the volones back to their standards (livy:en:25:20; recovery measures livy:en:25:22).

quote: ambassadors were sent to Hannibal to complain that Capua was abandoned, and almost given up to the Romans
notes: As the circumvallation closed, Capua sent ambassadors to reproach Hannibal for abandoning them, while scorning the Roman proclamation allowing Campanians to leave with their property before the ides of March (livy:en:25:22).

quote: the plot was reported to Epicydes, by one Attalus, who felt hurt that he had not been intrusted with the secret
notes: A conspiracy of some eighty Syracusans to betray the city to Marcellus was denounced by Attalus and all the plotters were tortured to death (livy:en:25:23).

quote: Having put them to death, they summoned the multitude to an assembly
notes: After agreeing on capitulation terms with Marcellus, the Sicilian envoys induced the besieged to kill Epicydes' prefects Polyclitus, Philistion and Sindon and then argued for surrender in a popular assembly (livy:en:25:28).

quote: hastily seizing their arms, they first put the praetors to death, and then ran through the city to massacre the Syracusans
notes: Fearing they would be handed over to Rome, the deserters stampeded the mercenaries into killing the newly elected Syracusan praetors and rampaging through the city, after which six praetors were chosen and the tumult subsided (livy:en:25:29).

quote: Mericus was moved by these suggestions, and when it was resolved upon to send ambassadors to Marcellus, he sent his brother among them
notes: The Spanish prefect Mericus, secretly won over through a countryman, contrived the distribution of guard posts so as to admit Roman troops at the Arethusa gate, delivering the Achradina and island (livy:en:25:30).

quote: the Syracusans, at length delivered from their fears, threw open the gates of the Achradina, and sent deputies to Marcellus
notes: The Syracusans opened the Achradina and surrendered to Marcellus, who gave the city to plunder while protecting pro-Roman houses, ending the pro-Carthaginian regime in Syracuse (livy:en:25:31).

quote: The Celtiberians, suddenly taking up their standards, marched away
notes: Hasdrubal bribed the chiefs of Cn. Scipio's twenty thousand Celtiberian auxiliaries to march home, a desertion that stranded the Roman army and preceded the deaths of both Scipios (livy:en:25:33).

quote: they unanimously conferred the supreme command upon Lucius Marcius
notes: After the Scipios' deaths the surviving Spanish armies irregularly elected the Roman knight Lucius Marcius as their general in a soldiers' assembly, an unprecedented army-conferred command (livy:en:25:37).

quote: It was considered as an injurious precedent for generals to be chosen by the armies
notes: Senate takes offence at Marcius styling himself propraetor after election by the army, withholds the title, and has the tribunes refer the Spanish command to the people (livy:en:26:2).

quote: Cneius Fulvius, therefore, before the day appointed for the comitia arrived, went into exile to Tarquinii, and the commons resolved that it was a legal exile.
notes: Tribune Sempronius Blaesus prosecutes Cn. Fulvius for losing his army in Apulia (begun at livy:en:26:2), escalates the charge to treason, and Fulvius escapes capital judgment by exile ratified at livy:en:26:3.

quote: The slaves and populace could neither endure the famine, nor send messengers to Hannibal through guards so closely stationed.
notes: Famine inside blockaded Capua drives its internal politics toward sallies, appeals to Hannibal, and eventual surrender; anchored at livy:en:26:4.

quote: Lesius, who complained that Capua was deserted and betrayed by its nobles, accepted the office of chief magistrate, being the last Campanian who held it.
notes: With Capuan nobles refusing office in the besieged city, the obscure Seppius Lesius becomes the last medixtuticus of Capua (livy:en:26:6).

quote: the whole city was thrown into a state of alarm by the running up and down of persons who made vague additions to what they heard
notes: News of Hannibal's march on Rome throws the city into tumult, with matrons at the shrines and the senate sitting permanently in the forum (livy:en:26:9).

quote: the senate decreed that Quintus Fulvius should have equal authority with the consuls, lest on entering the city his power should cease
notes: Constitutionally anomalous grant allowing the proconsul Fulvius to retain imperium inside the city during the emergency (livy:en:26:9).

quote: cried out that the Aventine was taken. This circumstance occasioned such confusion and terror
notes: A false alarm that the Aventine had fallen causes citizens to stone their own soldiers from the rooftops amid repeated baseless tumults (livy:en:26:10).

quote: it was resolved that all who had been dictators, consuls, or censors, should be invested with authority till such time as the enemy had retired from the walls
notes: Extraordinary emergency measure re-investing all former curule magistrates with authority to suppress tumults while Hannibal lay before Rome (livy:en:26:10).

quote: The people, rushing in crowds to the senate-house, compelled Lesius to assemble a senate, and openly threatened the nobles
notes: The starving Capuan populace forces the absentee nobles back into the senate to debate surrender, where Vibius Virrius urges suicide instead (livy:en:26:13).

quote: decreed and sent ambassadors to surrender Capua to the Romans. About twenty-seven senators, following Vibius Virrius to his home, partook of the banquet
notes: The Capuan senate votes to surrender to Rome while Virrius and about twenty-seven senators take poison at his banquet before the gates are opened (livy:en:26:14).

quote: took the letter, and without opening it put it into his bosom, and then commanded the crier to order the lictor to do his duty
notes: Fulvius scourges and beheads the Campanian senators at Teanum and Cales, pocketing the senate's letter unread, after which Jubellius Taurea kills himself at the tribunal (livy:en:26:15; variant versions at livy:en:26:16).

quote: Thus eighty principal members of the senate were put to death; and about three hundred of the Campanian nobles thrown into prison.
notes: Capua's leaders are executed or imprisoned and the city is stripped of magistrates, senate, and assembly, to be ruled by an annual Roman prefect (livy:en:26:16).

quote: not only every century, but every individual to a man, decided that Publius Scipio should be invested with the command in Spain
notes: With no established candidate daring to stand, the people elect the twenty-four-year-old privatus Scipio proconsul for Spain, then waver over his youth until his speech at livy:en:26:19; anchored at livy:en:26:18.

quote: As a middle course between the two opinions, it was resolved that he should enter the city in ovation.
notes: The senate debates and refuses Marcellus a triumph for Sicily, compromising on an ovation with a tribunician law granting him imperium for the day (livy:en:26:21); coded electoral-conflict as nearest type for an honors contest.

quote: incensed partly because they had not been taken from the province with their general, and partly because they had been forbidden to winter in towns
notes: Soldiers left in Sicily, embittered at their terms of service, verge on mutiny until the praetor Marcus Cornelius pacifies them by turns soothing and reproving (livy:en:26:21).

quote: Go back and vote again, and consider that you have a Punic war in Italy, and that the leader of your enemies is Hannibal.
notes: Manlius Torquatus refuses the consulship on grounds of blindness and compels the prerogative century to revote, producing the election of Marcellus and Laevinus (livy:en:26:22).

quote: the senate decreed that they should be vowed every year for the time to come. The same year several prodigies were seen and reported.
