notes: On the praetor Calpurnius' motion the games of Apollo are made a perpetual annual vow, in a chapter also recording prodigies, their expiation, and priestly replacements (livy:en:26:23).

quote: gave information that his masters, with five noble Campanian youths, whose parents had been executed by Fulvius, were the authors of the fire
notes: A fire set in several places around the forum is traced by a slave informer to Campanian nobles avenging Fulvius' executions; the convicted are punished and the informer freed and rewarded (livy:en:26:27).

quote: besought him, with tears, that they might be permitted to go to Rome to the senate
notes: Surviving Campanians surround the consul Laevinus begging leave to plead before the senate against Fulvius' severity, and are brought to Rome under oath (livy:en:26:27).

quote: affirming, that they would not only abandon, each of them, his native country, but all Sicily, if Marcellus should again go thither with command
notes: Sicilian deputies in mourning canvass the nobility against Marcellus receiving Sicily, and the consuls exchange provinces between themselves (livy:en:26:29).

quote: Of the two cities which have been captured this year, let Capua arraign Fulvius, and Syracuse Marcellus.
notes: The senate hears the Sicilians' charges over the sack of Syracuse and Marcellus' defence (livy:en:26:31), then confirms his acts while commending Syracuse to future care (livy:en:26:32); anchored at livy:en:26:30.

quote: Lucius Atilius, plebeian tribune, proposed to the people, on the recommendation of the senate, a bill to the following effect
notes: Because the Campanians were Roman citizens, a plebiscite empowers the senate to judge them, and detailed sentences of confiscation, sale, chains, and relocation follow at livy:en:26:34; anchored at livy:en:26:33.

quote: So great was the murmuring and indignation of the people, on account of this edict, that a leader, rather than matter, was wanting for an insurrection.
notes: The consular edict requiring private citizens to furnish and pay rowers provokes open refusal in the forum by a people exhausted by taxes, forcing the consuls to pause three days (livy:en:26:35).

quote: Let us, senators, bring into the treasury to-morrow all our gold, silver, and coined brass, each reserving rings for himself, his wife, and children
notes: Laevinus' scheme of voluntary contributions by senators, emulated by the equites and commons, supplies rowers and pay without edict or coercion, resolving the levy crisis of livy:en:26:35 (anchored livy:en:26:36).

quote: Dasius was the friend of Hannibal; Blasius, as far as he could do it with safety, promoted the Roman interest
notes: Factional rivalry between Salapia's two leading men ends with Blasius betraying the town and its five hundred Numidian horsemen to Marcellus despite Dasius' denunciation before Hannibal (livy:en:26:38).

quote: Nor did he brook the affront put upon him by this injurious treatment, but immediately sent secret messengers to Laevinus, to treat about delivering up Agrigentum.
notes: Hanno's jealous removal of Mutines from command drives the Numidians to seize a gate and betray Agrigentum to the Romans — internal army politics of the Punic side in Sicily (livy:en:26:40).

quote: As this contest began almost to assume the character of a mutiny
notes: The rival claims of a centurion and a marine to the mural crown at New Carthage bring legions and fleet to the brink of mutiny until Scipio crowns both (livy:en:26:48).

quote: A hundred and seventy Campanians, headed by the Blosii who were brothers, had formed a conspiracy to set fire to all these at one hour of the night
notes: Campanian plot to burn the Roman soldiers' huts at Capua was betrayed by a slave and suppressed by summary execution (livy:en:27:3).

quote: The consul refusing to submit to the people what lay in his own power, and forbidding the praetor to do so, the plebeian tribunes put the question
notes: Consul Laevinus clashed with senate and tribunes over who should be dictator for the elections, fled to Sicily, and Marcellus then named Quintus Fulvius dictator as the commons ordered (livy:en:27:5).

quote: it was hardly constitutional that a chief magistrate should be continued in office
notes: Tribunes threatened to block the election because dictator Fulvius was presiding over his own candidacy, until both sides agreed to abide by the senate's decision and Fulvius was elected (livy:en:27:6).

quote: the patricians denying that Caius Mamilius Vitulus, who was a plebeian candidate, ought to be allowed to stand
notes: Patricians contested a plebeian candidacy for chief curio, the matter passed from tribunes to senate to people, and Mamilius became the first plebeian chief curio (livy:en:27:8).

quote: On entering the senate, Lucius Licinius, the praetor, led him out; on which the flamen appealed to the tribunes of the people
notes: The flamen of Jupiter reclaimed the lapsed ancient privilege of a senate seat through tribunician adjudication, restoring the priesthood's political standing (livy:en:27:8).

quote: Twelve of these, for they all had embassies at Rome, told the consuls that they had not whence to furnish either men or money
notes: Twelve of the thirty Latin colonies refused to supply soldiers or money after ten years of levies, and within Book 27 the senate answered only with a tacit reproof while honoring the eighteen loyal colonies (anchor livy:en:27:9, continued 27:10).

quote: the vicesimary gold, which was preserved in the most sacred part of the treasury as a resource in cases of extreme exigency, should be drawn out
notes: Facing the colonies' default, the senate authorized drawing the sacrosanct vicesimary gold reserve from the treasury as an emergency war fund (livy:en:27:10).

quote: The choosing of the senate was delayed by a dispute which arose between the censors about the selection of a chief of the senate
notes: The new censors quarreled over naming the princeps senatus until Cornelius yielded and Fabius was chosen, after which eight senators were expelled and the Cannae equites degraded (livy:en:27:11).

quote: not only the bill for depriving him of his command was thrown out, but the following day he was created consul
notes: Tribune Bibulus's bill to strip Marcellus of his command, debated in the Flaminian circus after his harangues begun in livy:en:27:20, collapsed before Marcellus's self-defense and he was elected consul the next day (anchor livy:en:27:21).

quote: It was asserted that Servilius was not qualified to be plebeian tribune or aedile
notes: Servilius's eligibility for plebeian office was challenged on the ground that his father was alive in enemy hands, but no resolution is recorded in this chapter (livy:en:27:21).

quote: to propose to the people a law to the effect, that a vow should be made to perform these games on a stated day for ever
notes: In response to a pestilence, a law was carried fixing the Apollinarian games on a permanent annual date, converting an ad hoc vow into a standing institution (livy:en:27:23).

quote: seven of the principal senators, with their children, escaped before night, and before the guards were posted at the gates
notes: Fearing Arretium's defection first flagged in livy:en:27:21, Rome garrisoned the town and exacted 120 hostages from senators' children, seven leading senators fleeing before the guards were set (anchor livy:en:27:24).

quote: that the town should be guarded by a garrison, and that all the Tarentines should be kept within their walls
notes: The senate hotly debated punishing the recaptured Tarentines, with Fabius defending them, and deferred final judgment while imposing a garrison (livy:en:27:25).

quote: The case of Marcus Livius, prefect of the citadel of Tarentum, was also debated with no less warmth
notes: The senate split between censuring and rewarding the prefect whose negligence lost Tarentum but who held its citadel, finally remitting his case to the censors amid Fabius's barb that recovery would have been needless had it not been lost (livy:en:27:25).

quote: Titus Quinctius Crispinus, the consul, after having nominated Titus Manlius Torquatus dictator for the purpose of holding the election and celebrating the games, died of his wound
notes: With both consuls dead after the ambush, the dying Crispinus named Manlius Torquatus dictator to hold the elections and games, leaving the commonwealth in a manner orphan (livy:en:27:33).

quote: having withheld their pity from him when arrayed in a mourning garment and a criminal, they now forced upon him the white gown against his will
notes: Marcus Livius, long embittered and withdrawn after his condemnation by the people, was pressed over his own protests into the consulship beside his enemy Nero, the senate later brokering their reconciliation at Fabius's instance in livy:en:27:35 (anchor livy:en:27:34).

quote: The pontiffs also decreed, that thrice nine virgins should go through the city singing a hymn
notes: After the Frusino androgyne and the lightning stroke on Juno Regina's temple, the pontiffs instituted novel expiatory rites including a hymn by the poet Livius and a matrons' offering funded from their dowries (livy:en:27:37).

quote: After each people had stated their grounds of exemption, the exemption of none was allowed, as the enemy was in Italy, except those of Antium and Ostia
notes: The coastal settlers' claim of sacrosanct exemption from the levy was heard and overruled by the senate for all but Antium and Ostia, whose men were bound by oath to stay near home (livy:en:27:38).

quote: the consul Caius Claudius nominated as dictator his colleague Marcus Livius
notes: Marcus Livius was named dictator to hold the consular elections, appointing Quintus Caecilius master of the horse (quote at livy:en:28:10).

quote: to make inquiry what states of the Tuscans and Umbrians had formed schemes of revolt from the Romans
notes: The dictator was sent by senate decree to Etruria to investigate which states had plotted revolt to Hasdrubal during his invasion (quote at livy:en:28:10).

quote: the vestal, who had the guarding of it for that night, was scourged by the command of Publius Licinius the pontiff
notes: Amid a wave of prodigies the fire of Vesta went out and the negligent vestal was scourged by the pontiff, with expiatory victims and a supplication decreed (quote at livy:en:28:11).

quote: issued an edict that all who were citizens of Cremona and Placentia should return to those colonies before a certain day
notes: After ambassadors of Placentia and Cremona complained of Gallic raids and depopulation, the consuls by senate decree ordered the colonists back — colony restoration rather than a new foundation (quote at livy:en:28:11).

quote: Besides, a mutiny arose in the camp at Sucro. Here were eight thousand men, stationed as a guard
notes: During the rumour of Scipio's death eight thousand troops at Sucro mutinied over arrears of pay, expelled their tribunes and conferred command and fasces on the privates Albius and Atrius (quote at livy:en:28:24).

quote: called together their countrymen the Lacetani, and summoning the Celtiberian youth to arms, devastated in a hostile manner the territories of the Suessetanians and Sedetanians, allies of the Romans
notes: Mandonius and Indibilis, disappointed of ruling Spain, rose against Rome's allies on the rumour of Scipio's death, then abandoned the attempt when he proved alive (quote at livy:en:28:24; lapse at 28:25).

quote: sending collectors round to the tributary states, to give the soldiers hopes of soon receiving their pay
notes: Seven military tribunes soothed the mutineers' pay grievances while Scipio raised money from tributary states and summoned the army to Carthage for payment (quote at livy:en:28:25).

quote: a warm debate took place as to whether they should visit with punishment the originators only of the mutiny
notes: Scipio's council debated and condemned the thirty-five ringleaders only, who were then lured to lodgings, plied with wine and arrested by stratagem (quote at livy:en:28:26).

quote: They were tied to the stake, scourged with rods, and decapitated
notes: After Scipio's reconciliation speech the condemned ringleaders were executed before the terrified assembly, which then re-took the oath of allegiance and received its pay (quote at livy:en:28:29).

quote: they again summoned their countrymen to arms; and assembling the auxiliaries which had joined them before
notes: Hearing of the severity shown the mutineers, Mandonius and Indibilis feared like punishment and rose again with 20,000 foot, until crushed in battle and pardoned (quote at livy:en:28:31; defeat and settlement 28:33-34).

quote: Scipio having without difficulty regained the affection of his soldiers, both by his punctuality in discharging the arrears of pay to all
notes: Scipio closed the Sucro affair by paying arrears to guilty and innocent alike and in an assembly redirected the army against the Ilergetian rebels (quote at livy:en:28:32).

quote: falling prostrate before his knees, ascribed his conduct to the fatal frenzy of those times
notes: After defeat Mandonius appealed to Scipio's clemency; Scipio spared the rebels, left them their arms and hostages untouched, and imposed only a fine to pay the troops (quote at livy:en:28:34).

quote: all the centuries, with the strongest marks of attachment, named Publius Scipio as consul
notes: After the senate declined his claim to a triumph, Scipio was elected consul by every century amid record crowds already dooming Africa to him as his province (quote at livy:en:28:38).

quote: It being generally reported that Africa, as a new province, was destined for Publius Scipio without casting lots
notes: Fabius opened the great senate debate against assigning Scipio the African command, charging personal ambition over the public good; Scipio replied at 28:43-44 (quote at livy:en:28:40).

quote: I require of you, tribunes of the people, to support me in refusing to give my opinion
notes: Fulvius invoked the tribunes against Scipio's threatened appeal to the people; their ruling forced the question into the senate, which gave Scipio Sicily with leave to cross to Africa (quote at livy:en:28:45).

quote: Scipio, though he could not obtain leave to levy troops, a point which he did not urge with great eagerness
notes: The senate denied Scipio a regular levy for the African expedition but allowed volunteers and voluntary allied contributions for building his fleet (quote at livy:en:28:45).

quote: the quaestors were ordered to sell a district of the Campanian territory extending from the Grecian trench to the sea
notes: For want of war funds the quaestors sold confiscated Campanian public land with informer rewards, while the city praetor policed where Campanians were permitted to dwell (quote at livy:en:28:46).

quote: certain of the Sicilian horsemen felt a strong aversion to that service, as being severe and arduous
notes: Sicilian horsemen averse to African service are released by Scipio in exchange for equipping and training Roman substitutes (livy:en:29:1).

quote: restored their property to the Syracusans, partly by proclamation, and partly even by judgments pronounced against those who pertinaciously retained their unjust acquisitions
notes: Scipio enforces senate-granted restitution of Syracusan Greeks' property against Italian holders by edict and adjudication (livy:en:29:1).

quote: been driven out by the opposite faction, which had delivered up Locri to Hannibal
notes: Locrian exiles at Rhegium use ransomed artisans to conspire with Rome and betray the Locri citadel, reversing the rival faction's defection to Hannibal (livy:en:29:6).

quote: He inflicted punishment on the persons principally concerned, and gave their effects to the leaders of the other party
notes: After retaking Locri Scipio punishes the defection's ringleaders, transfers their property to the loyal faction, and remits the city's status to the senate (livy:en:29:8).

quote: not only were other temples violated, but even the treasures of Proserpine, which had never been touched through all ages
notes: Pleminius and his garrison plunder Locri and sack the untouched treasury of Proserpina's temple, a sacrilege Livy makes the root of the ensuing violence (livy:en:29:8).

quote: they made an attack upon the lieutenant-general, having first mutilated the lictors in a shocking manner
notes: Soldiers' factions fight over loot, Pleminius scourges the tribunes, and his own troops mutiny, mutilating the legate's nose and ears; Scipio's cognizance acquits Pleminius and chains the tribunes (livy:en:29:9).

quote: after lacerating them with every punishment which the human body could endure, put them to death
notes: Pleminius tortures the military tribunes to death, denies them burial, and kills Locrian nobles who had complained to Scipio (livy:en:29:9).

quote: if the Idaean Mother should be brought from Pessinus to Rome
notes: A Sibylline prophecy found by the decemviri, reinforced by Delphi, moves the senate to resolve on importing the Idaean Mother cult (livy:en:29:10).

quote: Quintus Caecilius Metellus was nominated dictator for holding the elections, by the consul in Bruttium
notes: With the sick consul unable to return, Q. Caecilius Metellus is named dictator to hold the elections and abdicates when they conclude; proposal at livy:en:29:10, nomination quoted at livy:en:29:11.

quote: The senate was occupied with the determination of a matter of no small importance, namely, who was the most virtuous man in the state
notes: The senate adjudges young Scipio Nasica the best man in the state to receive the Magna Mater, who is installed in the temple of Victory with the new Megalesian games (livy:en:29:14).

quote: the twelve Latin colonies which had refused to furnish soldiers to the consuls, Quintus Fabius and Quintus Fulvius
notes: The senate disciplines the twelve defaulting colonies with doubled levies, an annual one-per-thousand tax, and a Roman-style census, detaining their envoys until they comply (livy:en:29:15).

quote: the monies which had been contributed by private individuals, when he and Marcus Claudius were consuls, should now at length be repaid
notes: Laevinus moves repayment of citizens' wartime loans to the treasury; the senate decrees repayment in three instalments (livy:en:29:16).

quote: ten ambassadors of the Locrians, covered with filth, and in mourning, and extending branches of olive
notes: Ten Locrian suppliants prostrate themselves before the consuls in the comitium and are granted a senate hearing against Pleminius; their speech fills livy:en:29:17-18 (quote at livy:en:29:16).

quote: Pleminius should be conveyed to Rome in chains, and in chains plead his cause
notes: Fabius moves that Pleminius be tried in chains and that Scipio be recalled with his command abrogated; the vote stalls amid heated debate over Scipio's Greek habits (livy:en:29:19).

quote: the tribunes might direct to apprehend him, and bring him home in right of their most sacred authority
notes: On Metellus's motion the senate sends an extraordinary commission - praetor, ten deputies, two tribunes, and an aedile - to Locri, empowered to arrest even Scipio if implicated (livy:en:29:20).

quote: Pleminius, and as many as thirty-two persons with him, they condemned and sent in chains to Rome
notes: The commission restores the sacred money with expiation, returns Locrian liberty, laws, and property, and condemns Pleminius with thirty-two accomplices, sending them to Rome in chains (livy:en:29:21).

quote: Pleminius, however, died in prison, before the people had come to a determination respecting him
notes: Pleminius dies in prison before the people's verdict, while the commission's report vindicates Scipio and the senate votes him his crossing to Africa (livy:en:29:22).

quote: made an attempt, by means of certain persons whom he had corrupted by bribes, to set fire to the city in several places
notes: In Clodius Licinius's variant account Pleminius plots from prison to fire Rome to escape, and is consigned to the Tullianum by senate decree (livy:en:29:22).

quote: many of the Tuscan nobles, who had either themselves gone, or had sent others to Mago respecting the revolt of their states
notes: The consul Cornelius holds senate-decreed trials in Etruria, condemning nobles who intrigued with Mago, with absentees condemned in exile and their property confiscated (livy:en:29:36).

quote: Cneius Babius, tribune of the people, thinking this a favourable opportunity of advancing himself at their expense, summoned them both to trial before the people
notes: The censors Livius and Nero degrade each other's horse and Livius disfranchises thirty-four tribes, and the tribune Babius's attempted prosecution of both is quashed by the senate (livy:en:29:37).

quote: They established also a new tax out of the price of salt
notes: The censors institute a graduated salt tax, popularly read as Livius's revenge on the tribes that condemned him, earning him the surname Salinator (livy:en:29:37).

quote: They then received a census of the twelve colonies, which had never been done before
notes: The censors receive the first-ever census of the twelve colonies so their manpower and money resources stand in the public records, completing the enforcement decreed at livy:en:29:15 (quote at livy:en:29:37).

quote: Publius Scipio was continued in command for a period not limited in point of time
notes: Senate prorogues Scipio's African command without time limit, until the war's end, an unusual open-ended grant (livy:en:30:1).

quote: they sent thirty of their principal elders as deputies to solicit peace
notes: Carthaginian polity, dismayed by Syphax's capture, silences the war party and sends thirty elders to Scipio to solicit peace and a truce (livy:en:30:16).

quote: They requested that the senate would by a decree confirm the title of king with the other favours and benefits conferred by Scipio
notes: Masinissa's envoys appeal to the senate, which confirms his royal title, decrees presents, and releases Numidian captives (livy:en:30:17).

quote: Caius Servilius should be indemnified for having filled the offices of plebeian tribune and plebeian aedile contrary to what was established by the laws
notes: A plebiscite retroactively indemnifies the consul Servilius for office-holding that violated the law because his curule father was alive in captivity (livy:en:30:19).

quote: ambassadors from Saguntum arrived, bringing with them some Carthaginians who had crossed over into Spain for the purpose of hiring auxiliaries
notes: Saguntine allies appeal to the senate with captured Carthaginian recruiters and their gold; senate imprisons the men, returns the treasure, and rewards the envoys (livy:en:30:21).

quote: The ambassadors were dismissed without having accomplished the peace, and almost without an answer
notes: Senate debates the first Carthaginian peace embassy; Laevinus's view that they are spies prevails and the envoys are dismissed (livy:en:30:21-23, quote at livy:en:30:23).

quote: Publius Sulpicius, who was created dictator for this very purpose, recalled the consul to Italy, in virtue of his superior authority
notes: Consul Servilius crosses to Sicily unauthorized hoping to invade Africa, so a dictator is created expressly to recall him by superior imperium (livy:en:30:24).

quote: the people were yelling in the vestibule of the senate-house, lest so great a booty should escape from their hands and their sight
notes: Carthaginian polity: a crowd besieges the senate-house and a mixed assembly of senate and people votes to seize storm-driven Roman transports despite the truce (livy:en:30:24).

quote: distributed to the people, so much for each street, at the rate of four asses a bushel, a great quantity of corn which had been sent out of Spain
notes: Curule aediles distribute Spanish grain street by street at four asses a bushel, cheap-grain politics rather than a dispute proper (livy:en:30:26).

quote: being engaged, according to a decree of the senate, in making inquisitions respecting the conspiracies of the principal inhabitants
notes: The consul is detained in Etruria conducting senate-decreed inquisitions into conspiracies of leading Etruscans (livy:en:30:26).

quote: All the tribes nominated Publius Scipio. Nevertheless, the consuls put the province of Africa to the lot, for so the senate had decreed
notes: Both consuls seek Africa to supersede Scipio; the tribes unanimously back Scipio yet the senate still has the consuls cast lots, giving Claudius equal command (livy:en:30:27).

quote: Hannibal, indignant that such language should be held and listened to at such a juncture, laid hold of Gisgo with his own hand, and dragged him from his elevated position
notes: Carthaginian polity: Hannibal forcibly drags the anti-peace speaker Gisgo from the rostrum, then apologizes and argues the terms are necessary (livy:en:30:37).

quote: having nominated Caius Servilius Geminus as dictator, that he might not be recalled to the city to hold the elections
notes: Consul Servilius names Servilius Geminus dictator to hold the elections so he need not leave his province (livy:en:30:39).

quote: fresh ones were not appointed to succeed them, the state was without curule magistrates
notes: Weather repeatedly blocks the elections, outgoing magistrates retire leaving no curule magistrates, and two plebeian aediles abdicate over a flaw in their election (livy:en:30:39).

quote: found, on the testimony of an informer, to have privately conveyed money out of the treasury, and were condemned, not without disgrace to the aedile Lucullus
notes: Aediles' scribes and runners are convicted on an informer's evidence of stealing treasury money, disgracing the aedile Lucullus (livy:en:30:39).

quote: He therefore refused to allow any business to be transacted before the province of Africa was assigned him
notes: Consul Lentulus obstructs all public business demanding Africa; tribunes resist, and after disputes in senate and assembly the senate votes a compromise under oath (livy:en:30:40).

quote: they were told, that the king was seeking occasion for war, and that if he persisted he would soon obtain his object
notes: Philip's ambassadors are heard and dismissed with a warning that the king has doubly violated the treaty (livy:en:30:42).

quote: Cneius Lentulus, whose province the fleet was, protested against the decree of the senate
notes: Consul Lentulus blocks the senate's peace decree; tribunes carry the question to the people, and all tribes order Scipio to grant the peace and bring home the army (livy:en:30:43).

quote: Now, because a tribute is to be levied from private property, you lament with one accord, as though at the funeral of the state
notes: Carthaginian polity: struggling to raise the first indemnity instalment from private property, the senate laments and Hannibal's laughter provokes Hasdrubal Haedus's rebuke (livy:en:30:44).

quote: He was, doubtless, the first general who was distinguished by a name derived from the nation which he had conquered
notes: Scipio triumphs with unparalleled splendour and receives the surname Africanus, the first commander ever surnamed from his conquest, setting an honorific precedent (livy:en:30:45).

quote: appoint ten commissioners to survey, and distribute among them, that part of the Samnite and Apulian lands which was the property of the Roman people
notes: Senate decrees ager publicus in Samnium and Apulia for Scipio's African veterans and has the urban praetor name ten land commissioners; a land-settlement measure rather than agitation, hence the loose type fit (livy:en:31:4).

quote: a vast quantity of corn, which Scipio had sent from Africa, was distributed by them to the people
notes: Curule aediles distribute African grain sent by Scipio at four asses a peck; a subsidized distribution easing post-war food pressure rather than a scarcity crisis proper (livy:en:31:4).

quote: the proposal concerning the Macedonian war was rejected by almost all the tribes
notes: War-weary centuriate assembly, egged on by tribune Q. Baebius, rejects the senate's proposed declaration of war on Philip; senate rebukes the tribune and orders a new assembly (livy:en:31:6).

quote: After this speech of Sulpicius, being sent to give their votes, they declared for the war as he had proposed
notes: Re-vote after Sulpicius's speech in the Campus Martius reverses the earlier popular rejection and the centuries declare war on Philip (livy:en:31:8; speech in livy:en:31:7).

quote: but he was not empowered to take with him any veteran soldier against his will
notes: Reflecting veterans' resistance to re-enlistment after the Punic war, the senate restricts Sulpicius to volunteers from Scipio's returned African army and orders the veteran troops disbanded (livy:en:31:8).

quote: The pontiffs determined, that it could; and that it would be even more in order to do it in that way
notes: After the chief pontiff Licinius blocks the people's vow of games for the Macedonian war over funding, the pontifical college sanctions the first votive games vowed at an unspecified expense, a new religious-fiscal precedent (livy:en:31:9).

quote: if they wished for peace, they must recall him, and give him up to the Roman people
notes: After the Gallic revolt and sack of Placentia, the senate sends an embassy demanding Carthage recall and surrender Hamilcar, the Carthaginian leading the Gauls; Carthage answers with exile and confiscation (quote at livy:en:31:11; answer at livy:en:31:19).

quote: the people were particularly shocked at the hermaphrodites, which were ordered to be immediately thrown into the sea
notes: Mass religious alarm at prodigies (hermaphrodites, monstrous births) is expiated by decemviral rites, a hymn by thrice nine virgins, and an offering to Juno; coded loosely as popular tumult since the codebook has no prodigy-expiation type (livy:en:31:12).

quote: that an inquiry be made concerning the robbery of the treasury, according to the method used by Marcus Pomponius
notes: Senate orders the praetor in Bruttium to hold a formal inquiry into the theft from Proserpine's treasury at Locri on the Pleminius-era model; money is restored out of the effects of the guilty (quote at livy:en:31:12; outcome at livy:en:31:13).

quote: they should, therefore, have liberty to purchase any belonging to the public, and which lay within fifty miles of the city
notes: With the treasury empty for the new war, creditors owed the third installment of Punic-war loans protest confiscation by stealth; the senate's compromise assigns ager publicus within fifty miles at a nominal one-as rent (the trientabula) (livy:en:31:13).

quote: Against this, Tiberius Sempronius Longus, tribune of the people, protested
notes: Senate refuses proconsul Lentulus a triumph for Spain for lack of precedent and grants an ovation; tribune Sempronius Longus vetoes even that, then withdraws under unanimous senatorial pressure (livy:en:31:20).

quote: The elder part refused him a triumph, both because the army, with which he had acted, belonged to another
notes: Praetor Furius, rushing to Rome in the consul's absence, demands a triumph for his Gallic victory; after a divided senate debate he prevails and triumphs in office, and consul Aurelius later protests the unprecedented procedure (debate at livy:en:31:48; see 31:47 and 31:49); coded as the nearest type for an intra-elite honors contest.

quote: he should, for every year, receive two acres; and that ten commissioners should distribute that land
notes: Senate fixes the veteran settlement at two iugera per year served in Spain or Africa, to be distributed by the ten commissioners; implementation of the land grant decreed at 31:4 (livy:en:31:49).

quote: Three commissioners were then appointed to fill up the number of colonists at Venusia
notes: Triumviral commission enrolls supplementary colonists for Venusia, depleted in the Hannibalic war; a colony reinforcement rather than a new foundation (livy:en:31:49).

quote: distributed among the people a vast quantity of corn, brought from Africa, at the rate of two asses a peck
notes: In a year of remarkably cheap provisions the curule aediles distribute African grain at two asses a peck; abundance-driven distribution, not scarcity (livy:en:31:50).

quote: being flamen Dialis, could not take the oath of observing the laws; and no person was allowed to hold any office longer than five days
notes: Curule aedile-elect C. Valerius Flaccus, as flamen Dialis, cannot swear the magistrate's oath; senate, tribunes, and a plebiscite allow his brother to swear by proxy, and a parallel plebiscite recalls his absent colleague Cethegus from Spain (livy:en:31:50).

quote: that he might finish the inquiries concerning the conspiracies in Bruttium, which, while praetor, he had managed with care and fidelity
notes: Minucius's command is prorogued to complete the Bruttium conspiracy inquiries and punish the Locri sacrilege convicts (livy:en:32:1).

quote: The favour granted to the Narnians, of filling up their number of colonists, was refused to the people of Cossa
notes: Senate appoints triumvirs to adjust Narnia's colonist rolls after complaints of interlopers, while Cossa's parallel request is refused (livy:en:32:2).

quote: found the soldiers in a violent mutiny, which had been previously excited, and not sufficiently repressed at the commencement
notes: Two thousand veterans in Macedonia mutiny for discharge; Villius defuses it by promising to refer their release to the senate (livy:en:32:3).

quote: was hindered from entering the city in ovation by Marcus Portius Laeca, plebeian tribune, notwithstanding he had obtained permission of the senate
notes: Tribune Laeca vetoes Acidinus's senate-granted ovation on his return from Spain, forcing him to enter Rome as a private citizen (livy:en:32:7).

quote: who wished to hinder Titus Quinctius Flamininus from standing candidate for the consulship, after passing through the office of quaestor
notes: Tribunes Fulvius and Curius obstruct Flamininus's consular candidacy for skipping the cursus; the senate rules the people may elect whom they choose (livy:en:32:7).

quote: Five of them declared, that they would propose the question concerning an alliance with Rome, and would take the votes on it
notes: Achaean demiurgi split five-five over putting the Roman alliance to a vote, broken only when Rhisiasus threatens to kill his son Memnon (livy:en:32:22).

quote: the Dymaeans, Megalopolitans, with several of the Argives, rose up, and withdrew from the council
notes: Pro-Macedonian delegations secede from the Achaean council rather than vote for the Roman alliance, a step excused for their obligations to Philip (livy:en:32:22).

quote: the city of Argos was betrayed into his hands by some of the principal inhabitants, after they had first sounded the minds of the populace
notes: After the populace insists on restoring Philip's name to the herald's invocation, leading Argives betray the city to Philocles and the Achaean garrison is expelled (livy:en:32:25).

quote: Two slaves came to him before daylight, and disclosed to him in order the whole proceedings and intentions of the conspirators
notes: Slaves of the Carthaginian hostages plot to seize Setia, Norba and Circeii during the games; informers betray it and praetor Merula crushes it with a tumultuary levy, later executing some five hundred at Praeneste (livy:en:32:26).

quote: The services of the two who made the discovery, and of one free person employed, were highly meritorious
notes: The senate deploys the informer-reward instrument, granting the slave informers freedom plus twenty-five thousand asses each, their owners compensated from the treasury (livy:en:32:26).

quote: this year, for the first time, six praetors were appointed, in consequence of the increase of the provinces
notes: The praetorian college is expanded to six for the first time to cope with the empire's additional provinces (livy:en:32:27).

quote: deemed too severe in punishing usury. He drove the usurers entirely out of the island
notes: As praetor of Sardinia Cato punishes usury harshly, expelling the moneylenders and cutting the allies' contributions for praetorian upkeep (livy:en:32:27).

quote: Lucius Oppius and Quintus Fulvius, plebeian tribunes, stood in their way, alleging, that Macedonia was a very distant province
notes: Tribunes Oppius and Fulvius block the consular lot for Macedonia; the senate assigns both consuls Italy and prorogues Quinctius's command (livy:en:32:28).

quote: Caius Acilius, plebeian tribune, caused an order to be passed, that five colonies should be led out to the sea-coast
notes: Tribune Acilius carries a measure founding five maritime colonies of three hundred families each, with triumvirs appointed for three years (livy:en:32:29).

quote: a violent dissension broke out at Opus. One faction invited to their assistance the Aetolians, who were nearest at hand; the other, the Romans
notes: Rival factions at Opus each appeal to an outside power; the stronger pro-Roman party shuts out the Aetolians and holds the city for Quinctius (livy:en:32:32).

quote: Nabis was admitted into the city in the night, without the privity of any of the inhabitants
notes: Philip entrusts Argos to Nabis, who is let in by night, seizes the heights, and plunders the citizens under exorbitant contributions (livy:en:32:38).

quote: one for an abolition of debts, the other for a distribution of the land, in shares, to each man
notes: Nabis proclaims debt abolition and land redistribution at Argos, the two firebrands for inflaming the populace against the higher ranks (livy:en:32:38).

quote: the consuls, overcome by the obstinacy of the tribunes, proposed their claims separately
notes: Tribunes Atinius Labeo and Ursanius blocked a joint triumph for the consuls for two days until they agreed to separate votes (livy:en:33:22).

quote: declared, that by the authority of his office of consul, and pursuant to the example of many illustrious men, he would triumph on the Alban mount
notes: Continuation of the triumph dispute: the senate granted Cornelius a triumph but refused Minucius, who then triumphed on the Alban Mount by his own consular authority (livy:en:33:23).

quote: praying that the number of their colonists might be enlarged; an order was accordingly passed, that one thousand should be added to the list
notes: On petition of Cossa the senate ordered 1,000 new colonists enrolled, excluding former partisans of the enemy (livy:en:33:24).

quote: they would enter their protest, unless they were allowed, before any further proceeding, to take the sense of the people
notes: Consul Marcellus sought Macedonia as a province hoping to renew the war, but tribunes threatened a veto until the people voted, and all 35 tribes ratified the peace with Philip (livy:en:33:25).

quote: a conspiracy among the slaves had well nigh made Etruria an hostile province
notes: Praetor Acilius Glabrio was sent with a city legion to crush a slave conspiracy in Etruria, scourging and crucifying the ringleaders (livy:en:33:36).

quote: for the first time, were created offices called triumviri epulones
notes: A tribunician law of C. Licinius Lucullus created the new priestly board of triumviri epulones, granted the purple-bordered gown (livy:en:33:42).

quote: The body of the pontiffs had this year a warm dispute with the city quaestors
notes: To fund the final repayment of citizens' war loans the quaestors exacted arrears of wartime contributions from priests, whose appeal to the tribunes failed (livy:en:33:42); coded debt-crisis for want of a fiscal-dispute type.

quote: made a distribution to the people of one million pecks of wheat, at the price of two asses
notes: Curule aediles distributed cheap Sicilian grain to the people as a political benefaction, not a shortage dispute (livy:en:33:42); included low-confidence as grain politics.

quote: brought many farmers of the public pastures to trial before the people. Three of these were convicted
notes: Plebeian aediles prosecuted lessees of public pastures before the people; fines from three convictions funded a temple of Faunus (livy:en:33:42).

quote: Persons of the faction which opposed Hannibal wrote continually to their several friends, among the principal men in Rome
notes: Carthaginian polity: Hannibal's domestic enemies appealed to leading Romans with charges of collusion with Antiochus, prompting Roman intervention despite Scipio Africanus's opposition (livy:en:33:45, continued 33:47).

quote: he proposed a law, and procured it to be enacted, that the judges should be elected annually
notes: Carthaginian polity: as sufete (praetor) Hannibal broke the life-tenured order of judges by carrying a law for annual election with no iteration (livy:en:33:46).

quote: if payment were enforced of the residuary funds, the taxes might be remitted to the subjects
notes: Carthaginian polity: Hannibal audited and reclaimed embezzled public revenues so the Roman tribute could be paid without a new tax, enraging the profiteering elite (livy:en:33:47).

quote: In this manner did Hannibal leave Africa, lamenting the misfortunes of his country oftener than his own
notes: Carthaginian polity: under Roman pressure engineered by his domestic enemies Hannibal fled into exile, ending his reform ascendancy amid factional turmoil in the forum (livy:en:33:48); regime-change coded low as nearest type for the fall of the leading statesman.

quote: nor could the matrons be kept at home, either by advice or shame, nor even by the commands of their husbands
notes: Phase 1 of the Lex Oppia repeal struggle at livy:en:34:1: matrons fill the streets and Capitol to press for repeal of the sumptuary law while two tribunes threaten veto.

quote: the women next day poured out into public in much greater numbers, and in a body beset the doors of the tribunes
notes: Phase 2 at livy:en:34:8: after the Cato-Valerius debate the matrons escalate, blockading the houses of the vetoing tribunes until they yield.

quote: nor did they retire until this intervention was withdrawn
notes: Resolution phase at livy:en:34:8: the Bruti withdraw their tribunician veto under crowd pressure and all tribes vote the Oppian law's repeal, twenty years after enactment.

quote: he settled the iron and silver mines on such a footing, that they produced a large revenue
notes: At livy:en:34:21 Cato institutes a new fiscal regime for the Spanish iron and silver mines, a provincial-revenue reform credited with enriching the province; marginal as a domestic event.

quote: laid claim to a privilege unheard of before; that Latins, giving in their names for a Roman colony, should be deemed citizens of Rome
notes: At livy:en:34:42 Ferentinate Latins enrolled for citizen colonies claim Roman citizenship, an unprecedented privilege the senate rejects; coded as an attempted (failed) institutional innovation.

quote: procured men who were to set fire by night to several parts of the city at once
notes: At livy:en:34:44 the imprisoned Pleminius plots nocturnal arson across Rome to cover a prison break; accomplices inform, the senate is told, and he is summarily put to death in the lower dungeon.

quote: they ordered the curule aediles to set apart places for the senators, distinct from those of the people
notes: At livy:en:34:44 the censors institute segregated senatorial seating at the Roman games, ending promiscuous seating and winning the senate's gratitude.

quote: In this year colonies of Roman citizens were settled at Puteoli, Vulturnum, and Liternum; three hundred men in each place
notes: At livy:en:34:45 citizen colonies are planted at Puteoli, Vulturnum, Liternum, Salernum, Buxentum, Sipontum, Tempsa and Croto on confiscated Campanian and other lands under triumviral commissions.

quote: proposed to the people, and the people ordered, that two Latin colonies should be settled, one in Bruttium
notes: At livy:en:34:53 the tribune Tubero, on a senate decree, carries a plebiscite founding two Latin colonies in Bruttium and the Thurine territory, with three-year commissioners elected in the Capitol.

quote: the senators, for the first time, sat separate from the people, which, as every innovation usually does, gave occasion to various observations
notes: Implementation/controversy phase at livy:en:34:54: first separate senatorial seating at the games divides opinion as an affront to liberty and concord, and Africanus reportedly regrets it.

quote: the consuls, by direction of the senate, published an edict, that, on any day whereon religious rites should be ordered
notes: At livy:en:34:55 incessant earthquake reports paralyze public business until, after a three-day supplication, the consuls' edict forbids reporting a new earthquake on a day already under expiatory rites.

quote: made application to the plebeian tribunes, to take cognizance of the cases of such men as claimed exemption from the service
notes: At livy:en:34:56 soldiers resist the Ligurian emergency levy by appealing to the tribunes for exemptions until the senate votes a Gallic tumultus, barring tribunician cognizance of the claims.

quote: decrees of the senate were not to be passed in consequence of rumours fabricated by private persons for the gratification of magistrates
notes: Senate elders refuse Flaminius a city legion raised on privately circulated rumours, voting instead for tumultuary levies outside Italy (livy:en:35:2).

quote: rather than Quintus Minucius should be called away from a war, in which no progress had been made, to suffer an interregnum
notes: Senate threatens to let an interregnum occur unless consul Cornelius returns to hold the elections, and he yields (livy:en:35:6).

quote: a fraudulent course had been adopted —that of transferring the securities to subjects of some of the allied states
notes: Creditors evade Roman interest laws by channelling loans through allied citizens, overwhelming debtors with unlimited usury until the senate orders registration of such loans (livy:en:35:7).

quote: Marcus Sempronius, plebeian tribune, by direction of the senate, proposed to the people, and the people ordered
notes: Tribune Marcus Sempronius carries a law making loans between Romans and allies subject to the same usury rules as between citizens, closing the loophole (livy:en:35:7).

quote: the plebeian tribunes, Marcus and Caius Titinius, declared, that they would enter their protest, if the senate passed any decree on the subject
notes: Metellus blocks consul Merula's demand for a thanksgiving and triumph over the Boii, citing Marcellus's contradictory letters, and the tribunes Titinii threaten their protest (livy:en:35:8).

quote: a Latin colony was established in the Thurian territory by commissioners appointed for the purpose
notes: Commissioners settle a Latin colony of 3,000 foot and 300 horse in the Thurian territory, reserving a third of the land for future colonists (livy:en:35:9).

quote: with regard to the election of consuls, emulation was more fiercely kindled than was ever known before
notes: The fiercest consular canvass yet seen pits the brothers of Flamininus and Africanus against each other; Quinctius wins and Africanus fails even to carry Laelius (livy:en:35:10).

quote: They prosecuted to conviction many of the farmers of the public pastures
notes: The aediles Lepidus and Paulus convict many graziers of the public pastures and spend the fines on gilded shields and porticoes (livy:en:35:10).

quote: ambassadors should be sent to each of the kings; not only to sound their dispositions
notes: At the Naupactum assembly the Aetolian praetor Thoas carries a motion to send envoys to Nabis, Philip and Antiochus to stir them to war with Rome (livy:en:35:12).

quote: others, who more firmly adhered to the alliance with Rome, he put to death
notes: Nabis's emissaries sow dissension in the Laconian coastal towns, bribing some leading men and killing those loyal to the Roman alliance (livy:en:35:13).

quote: his father, thinking that his heir trod too closely on the heels of his own old age, had him taken off by poison
notes: Seleucid, not Roman: the death of Antiochus's heir is popularly blamed on the king himself as a dynastic poisoning by eunuchs (livy:en:35:15).

quote: There was, this year also, a warm competition, three patricians suing for one place
notes: With war looming the senate recalls the consul for early elections; after a warm three-way patrician contest Scipio, rejected the year before, is returned (livy:en:35:24).

quote: they summoned a council at Sicyon, and also sent deputies to Titus Quinctius to ask his advice
notes: The Achaean council at Sicyon, after consulting Rome and Quinctius, unanimously votes war on Nabis, leaving its conduct to the praetor Philopoemen (livy:en:35:25).

quote: Eurylochus, a deputy of the Magnetians, and others of that faction, wished for a total change of measures
notes: At the Magnetian council in Demetrias the Magnetarch Eurylochus's faction, fearing the city's return to Philip, courts Antiochus and the Aetolians; the clash drives him into exile (livy:en:35:31, flight in 35:32).

quote: a decree was passed that Antiochus should be invited to vindicate the liberty of Greece
notes: With Quinctius still present, the Aetolian council decrees that Antiochus be invited to free Greece and arbitrate between Aetolia and Rome (livy:en:35:33).

quote: making themselves masters of Demetrias, Chalcis, and Lacedaemon
notes: The Aetolian Apocleti secretly scheme to seize Demetrias, Chalcis and Lacedaemon, despatching Diocles, Thoas and Alexamenus respectively (livy:en:35:34).

quote: parties were sent to the houses of persons of the opposite faction, to put them to death
notes: Diocles's cavalry restores the exile Eurylochus and murders the opposing faction, delivering Demetrias into Aetolian hands (livy:en:35:34).

quote: their points at length penetrated his body, so that, before relief could be sent from the centre, he expired
notes: Alexamenus and the Aetolian horsemen Nabis had invited as allies cut the tyrant down during a review outside Sparta (livy:en:35:35).

quote: him they mounted on a horse, and taking arms, slew all the Aetolians whom they met straggling through the city
notes: The Spartans rally around the boy Laconicus, massacre the plundering Aetolians and kill Alexamenus, after which Philopoemen attaches Lacedaemon to the Achaean League (livy:en:35:36).

quote: he had engaged a party, composed of Euthymidas's faction, to betray the city into his hands
notes: Thoas's plan to have the exiled Euthymidas's partisans betray Chalcis miscarries when the magistrates learn of it and summon Eretrian and Carystian aid (livy:en:35:37, foiled in 35:38).

quote: In this year a colony was settled at Vibo, in pursuance of a decree of the senate and an order of the people
notes: A citizen colony of 3,700 foot and 300 horse is planted at Vibo on former Bruttian land, with fifteen acres per footman (livy:en:35:40).

quote: Many severe sentences were passed this year on usurers, who were prosecuted, as private persons, by the curule aediles
notes: The curule aediles Tuccius and Brutus win severe sentences against usurers and dedicate gilded chariots and bucklers on the Capitol from the fines (livy:en:35:41).

quote: the council voted, that the title of general should be conferred on the king
notes: After Thoas defeats Phaeneas's plea to use Antiochus as mediator rather than war-leader, the Aetolian council names the king their general with a council of thirty (livy:en:35:45).

quote: Apollodorus, the principal adviser of a revolt, being publicly charged therewith by one Leon, was condemned and driven into exile
notes: With Athens near civil war over largess-fed agitation for Antiochus, Apollodorus is condemned and exiled on Leon's charge after Quinctius intervenes (livy:en:35:50).

quote: Those who adhered to the Roman interest, on the approach of the king, withdrew from the city
notes: Under Antiochus's threats Chalcis opens its gates despite Mictio and Xenoclides, the pro-Roman party withdraws, and all Euboea submits to the king (livy:en:35:51).

quote: Was it their will, and did they order, that war should be undertaken against king Antiochus, and all who should join his party?
notes: Comitial war-declaration vote against Antiochus gated on religious preliminaries (sacrifices and favourable auspices ordered by the senate); no v1 type covers a war vote, so coded as formal institutional act; quote at livy:en:36:1.

quote: when they were impressed for manning the ships, they appealed to the tribunes of the people, by whom the cause was referred to the senate
notes: Eight maritime colonies (Ostia, Fregenae, etc.) resisted naval impressment and appealed to the tribunes; the senate unanimously denied their claimed exemption; quote at livy:en:36:3.

quote: no senator, nor any who had the privilege of giving an opinion in the senate, nor any of the inferior magistrates, should go so far from the city
notes: Wartime consular edict restricting senators' absence from Rome (no more than five absent at once) to keep the political class mobilized for the Antiochene war; quote at livy:en:36:3.

quote: The Eleans requested aid against the Achaeans; for they supposed, that, since the war had been declared against Antiochus contrary to their judgment
notes: Elis, fearing Achaean attack, appealed to Antiochus, who sent 1,000 foot under Euphanes the Cretan, while the Epirots sent a deliberately hedging embassy; quote at livy:en:36:5.

quote: a decree, disguised under a slight covering of words, was passed in his favour against the Romans
notes: The Boeotian national council, whose polity Livy says was in long socioeconomic decline with many hoping for a change of affairs, voted a veiled decree admitting Antiochus against Rome; quote at livy:en:36:6.

quote: Mnasilochus, a man of distinction among the Acarnanians, being bribed by many presents, not only laboured himself to dispose that nation in favour of the king
notes: Bribed Acarnanian notables Mnasilochus and the praetor Clytus plotted to betray Medio and Thurium to Antiochus; Medio fell by treachery (36:12) but Thurium held and Octavius' arrival steadied the loyalists; quote at livy:en:36:11.

quote: He, therefore, with his wife and children, quitted the kingdom, and retired to Ambracia. Thus all Athamania came under the authority and dominion of Philip.
notes: King Amynander fled to Ambracia as Philip's calculated clemency toward Athamanian prisoners swung his subjects' loyalty, and Athamania passed under Macedonian control; quote at livy:en:36:14.

quote: to request the king again to assemble his land and marine forces and cross over into Greece
notes: The Aetolian council at Hypata sent Thoas and other ambassadors to beg Antiochus to return with his forces or at least supply men and money, which he immediately provided; quote at livy:en:36:26.

quote: their minds were so highly exasperated, both by the harshness of the order and the indignity offered
notes: Though the Apocleti counselled submission after the consul's chains episode (36:28), the Aetolian general assembly, inflamed by Rome's harsh terms and Nicander's assurances of aid from Antiochus, repudiated peace; quote at livy:en:36:29.

quote: the Messenians were willing, both to open their gates, and surrender their city, to the Romans, but not to the Achaeans
notes: Besieged by the Achaeans for refusing to join their confederacy, Messene appealed over their heads to Quinctius, who ordered the siege raised, the exiles recalled, and Messene joined to the league on his arbitration; quote at livy:en:36:31.

quote: Phaeneas himself, with some others of the principal men, instantly came and threw themselves at his feet
notes: The besieged Aetolians at Naupactum appealed as suppliants to Quinctius, who interceded with the consul to grant a truce and allow an Aetolian embassy to surrender to the senate at Rome; quote at livy:en:36:35.

quote: a fast ought to be instituted in honour of Ceres, and the same observed every fifth year
notes: Prodigies (oxen climbing a roof, stone showers, lightning strikes) led the senate to order consultation of the Sibylline books, instituting a new quinquennial fast of Ceres plus supplications and expiatory sacrifices; quote at livy:en:36:37.

quote: The unanimous senate not only gave their vote for the triumph, but by their influence prevailed on the tribune to desist from his protest.
notes: Tribune Sempronius Blaesus moved to postpone Scipio Nasica's Boian triumph until Liguria was subdued (36:39), but after Scipio's rebuttal the senate voted the triumph and induced the tribune to drop his protest; quote at livy:en:36:40.

quote: the elections were held at Rome, in which were chosen consuls, Lucius Cornelius Scipio and Caius Laelius, from whom all men expected the conclusion of the war
notes: Year-end consular and praetorian elections framed by the expectation that the new consuls would finish the Antiochene war; no overt contest narrated here, coded for the electoral stakes of the eastern command; quote at livy:en:36:45.

quote: After it had been contested several days, it was at last resolved, that peace should neither be granted nor refused.
notes: Aetolian ambassadors supplicate the senate for peace; after days of contested debate the senate dictates harsh alternatives and orders them out of Italy (livy:en:37:1).

quote: Publius Scipio Africanus said, that if they decreed that province to his brother, Lucius Scipio, he would go along with him, as his lieutenant-general
notes: Consuls Laelius and L. Scipio both contest the Greek command until Africanus's offer to serve as legate swings the senate to his brother (livy:en:37:1); coded as electoral-conflict for command-assignment dispute.

quote: that the fleet was going off to a distance from Ephesus, from the war which concerned themselves
notes: Discontented talk among the military tribunes over the Patara expedition reaches and sways the praetor Aemilius, who turns the fleet back to Samos (livy:en:37:17); grumbling that shaped command, not an actual mutiny.

quote: the answer given to Antiochus was, that they could not treat of peace before the arrival of the consul
notes: Antiochus's first peace overture is debated in Aemilius's council at Elaea, where Eumenes argues no treaty is valid without consul, senate, and people (livy:en:37:19).

quote: But rage and avarice were too strong for his authority
notes: Roman soldiers plunder surrendered Phocaea against the praetor's explicit orders, and Aemilius can only salvage his pledge by protecting free persons in the forum (livy:en:37:32); army-politics breakdown of command.

quote: These concessions, which appeared to the ambassador of great moment towards obtaining a peace, the Romans deemed trifling
notes: Antiochus's envoy Heraclides offers terms in full council and privately tries to bribe Africanus with gold and his captive son, but the Romans demand cession beyond Taurus and talks collapse (quote at livy:en:37:35; bribe attempt in 37:36).

quote: Resign all pretensions in Europe, and cede that part of Asia which lies on this side of Mount Taurus
notes: After Magnesia, Antiochus's envoys accept whatever terms the Romans dictate; Africanus delivers the conditions in council at Sardis and the matter is referred to ambassadors at Rome (livy:en:37:45).

quote: the senate refused a triumph to Minucius, but, with great unanimity, decreed one to Acilius
notes: Rival triumph claims from returning proconsuls are decided by the senate, which denies Minucius and grants Acilius a triumph over Antiochus and the Aetolians (livy:en:37:46); coded electoral-conflict as closest type for a contested honors grant.

quote: the senate decreed, that Caius Laelius, the consul, if he thought proper, should enrol six thousand families, to be distributed among these colonies
notes: Deputies of Placentia and Cremona complain of depopulation and the senate decrees six thousand supplementary colonist families with commissioners to conduct them (livy:en:37:46).

quote: Marcus Aemilius Lepidus sought the office under general censure, for having, in order to sue for the office, left his province of Sicily
notes: Hotly contested consular election in which Lepidus canvasses under censure for leaving Sicily without leave and is rejected when Fulvius, elected alone, names Manlius colleague (livy:en:37:47).

quote: that the Aetolian ambassadors should be ordered to leave the city that day, and to quit Italy within fifteen days
notes: A second Aetolian embassy offends the senate with insolent recitals of past services and is expelled from Rome and Italy by decree on Acilius's motion (livy:en:37:49).

quote: At last religion prevailed, so that the flamen obeyed the order of the pontiff; and the fines were remitted by order of the people
notes: The chief pontiff detains the flamen-praetor Fabius Pictor from his Sardinian province, producing stormy deadlock in senate and before the commons with fines, tribunician appeals, and an attempted abdication (livy:en:37:51); veto-deadlock is the nearest type for this inter-magistrate jurisdictional standoff.

quote: The senate voted, that the peace should be observed; and the people, a few days after, ordered it
notes: After hearing Eumenes, Smyrna, the Rhodians, and Antiochus's envoys, senate and people ratify Scipio's peace and appoint ten commissioners to apportion Asia (livy:en:37:55; hearings span 37:52-56).

quote: Lucius Valerius Flaccus, Marcus Atilius Serranus, and Lucius Valerius Tappo, triumvirs, settled a Latin colony at Bononia, according to a decree of the senate
notes: Triumvirs plant a Latin colony of three thousand at Bononia on land confiscated from the Boian Gauls, with graded allotments for horsemen and other colonists (livy:en:37:57).

quote: commenced a prosecution against him, on a charge, that he had neither exhibited in his triumph, nor lodged in the treasury, a large part of the royal treasure
notes: Tribunes prosecute the censorial front-runner Glabrio for embezzling Antiochene booty, with Cato's testimony decisive, until Glabrio withdraws his candidacy and the tribunes drop the fine (livy:en:37:58).

quote: In the same year, many distinguished men strove for the censorship
notes: Violent nobiles-versus-new-man contest for the censorship, inflamed by Glabrio's largesses and prosecution, ends with Flamininus and Marcellus elected censors (livy:en:37:58).

quote: There were some who judged that the war was greater by fame than by real difficulty
notes: The senate votes Regillus a naval triumph and L. Scipio, now styling himself Asiaticus, a triumph, amid detractors belittling the Asian victory's difficulty (livy:en:37:59); coded electoral-conflict as nearest type for contested honors.

quote: out of money raised by fines on corn merchants, for raising the market by hoarding the grain
notes: Curule aediles fine grain merchants for hoarding to raise prices and dedicate gilded shields from the proceeds (livy:en:38:35).

quote: after having, this year, procured the rejection of his enemy, Marcus. Aemilius Lepidus
notes: Presiding consul Fulvius engineers the defeat of his personal enemy Lepidus at the consular elections (livy:en:38:35).

quote: When four tribunes of the commons were protesting against the bill, because it was not made under the direction of the senate
notes: Tribune Valerius Tappus carries full voting rights for Formiae, Fundi and Arpinum after four fellow tribunes drop their protest that the senate was bypassed (livy:en:38:36).

quote: petitioned that they might be allowed to take in marriage women who were citizens of Rome
notes: Campanians, now registered in the census at Rome (cf. livy:en:38:28), win rights of marriage with Roman citizens and legitimacy for existing children (livy:en:38:36).

quote: charged with having beaten the Carthaginian ambassadors, were, by order of Marcus Claudius, city praetor, delivered up by heralds to the ambassadors
notes: Two Romans charged with assaulting Carthaginian envoys are surrendered by the fetials to Carthage by order of the city praetor (livy:en:38:42).

quote: it would be highly indecorous to shut up the consuls among the valleys of Liguria, while Marcus Fulvius and Cneius Manlius reigned
notes: Consul Lepidus protests the prorogation of Fulvius and Manlius as quasi-regal; the senate keeps Liguria for the consuls but orders the proconsuls home (livy:en:38:42).

quote: he introduced to the senate ambassadors from Ambracia, whom he had secretly instructed in the charges they were to make against him
notes: Lepidus coaches Ambracian envoys to accuse his enemy Fulvius before the senate, which in Flaminius's absence decrees restitution and that Ambracia was not taken by force (livy:en:38:43, cf. 38:44).

quote: the greater number of the ten ambassadors, who had been in the province along with him, opposed the grant
notes: Manlius Vulso's own commission opposes his triumph, forcing him to defend his Galatian war before the senate (livy:en:38:44), which finally votes the triumph in 38:50.

quote: The two Petillii, as Valerius Antias writes, instituted a prosecution against Publius Scipio Africanus
notes: Tribunician prosecution of Africanus opens the Scipionic trials; his speech on his exploits dominates the first day (livy:en:38:50).

quote: the whole assembly turned about and followed him; insomuch, that at last even the clerks and messengers left the tribunes
notes: On the anniversary of Zama Scipio leads the entire assembly away from his judges to the Capitol, a walkout the tribunes themselves brand a secession in livy:en:38:52 (quote at livy:en:38:51).

quote: he retired to the territory of Liternum, with a fixed determination not to attend the trial
notes: Africanus withdraws to Liternum refusing to stand trial; Lucius pleads his sickness and the tribunes adjourn the case (livy:en:38:52).

quote: he would not suffer Publius Scipio to be accused until he should return to Rome
notes: Gracchus, Scipio's personal enemy, uses tribunician power to shield him; the prosecution lapses and the senate thanks Gracchus (livy:en:38:53).

quote: Servius Sulpicius, the city praetor, shall ask the senate which of the present praetors they will appoint to hold an inquiry
notes: After Africanus's death the Petillian plebiscite, backed by Cato who talks the Mummii out of their veto, creates a special inquiry into Antiochus's money (livy:en:38:54).

quote: Scipio and Aulus Hostilius, his lieutenant-general, and Caius Furius, were convicted on the following charges
notes: Before the praetor Terentius Culleo, Lucius Scipio, his legate and his quaestor are convicted of taking bribes from Antiochus (livy:en:38:55).

quote: he tore it to pieces in the view of the senate, at the same time expressing indignation at being called to account for four millions
notes: Africanus destroys the account books before the senate rather than account for four million sesterces after bringing two hundred million into the treasury (livy:en:38:55).

quote: he drove away the officer from his person; and, on the tribunes attempting to detain him, laid violent hands on them
notes: In the variant tradition Livy reports, Africanus violently frees his brother from arrest and assaults the tribunes, which Gracchus denounces as annulling tribunician power (livy:en:38:56).

quote: he had not in his possession any thing whatever belonging to the public, was ordered to prison
notes: Refusing securities on the ground that all the money is in the treasury, Lucius Scipio is ordered to prison and Nasica appeals to the tribunes with a defense of the Cornelii (livy:en:38:58, speech continues in 38:59).

quote: in chains, he never would suffer; and therefore he ordered him to be discharged
notes: Alone among the tribunes Gracchus forbids imprisonment while allowing execution on the estate; the seizure and sale of Lucius Scipio's property fails to cover the fine and he refuses the contribution raised by friends (livy:en:38:60).

quote: The Caenomanians complained of this to the senate at Rome, and were by them referred to the consul Aemilius
notes: Disarmed Cenomani appeal to the senate against the praetor Furius, who is ordered to restore their arms and quit the province (livy:en:39:3).

quote: In consequence of this inquiry, twelve thousand Latins returned home; as the multitude of foreigners even then burdened the city.
notes: Latin confederate envoys protest migration of their citizens to Rome; praetorian inquiry compels twelve thousand Latins to return home (livy:en:39:3).

quote: Marcus Abutius, a tribune of the commons, gave notice, that, if any thing were determined on that subject before the arrival of Marcus Aemilius, he would enter his protest
notes: Tribune Abutius, acting for the absent consul Aemilius, threatens veto of Fulvius' triumph until his colleague Gracchus shames him into withdrawing and the triumph is voted (quote at livy:en:39:4; resolution in 39:5).

quote: The reason of his deferring his triumph so long was, to avoid standing a trial under the Petillian law
notes: Manlius Vulso delays his Asian triumph to escape prosecution under the Petillian law amid the fallout of Lucius Scipio's condemnation (livy:en:39:6).

quote: The following year diverted Spurius Postumius Albinus and Quintus Marcius Philippus, from the care of armies, and wars, and provinces, to the punishing of an intestine conspiracy.
notes: The Bacchanalian cult spreading from Etruria is framed as an intestine conspiracy and both consuls are assigned the inquisition into clandestine meetings (livy:en:39:8).

quote: Their number was exceedingly great now, almost a second state in themselves, and among them were many men and women of noble families.
notes: The freedwoman informer Hispala, under consular promise of protection, discloses the cult's scale and crimes, describing it as almost a second state (quote at livy:en:39:13; testimony begins 39:12).

quote: They then commit to the consuls the holding an inquiry, out of the common course, concerning the Bacchanals and their nocturnal orgies.
notes: Senate erects an extraordinary inquisition with informer rewards, Italy-wide proclamation, night watches, and protection for Aebutius and Fecenia - a full accusation apparatus (livy:en:39:14).

quote: Above seven thousand men and women are said to have taken the oath of the association.
notes: After the consular edict terror spreads through Italy; fugitives are seized at the gates, suicides follow, and the chief priests of the sect confess (livy:en:39:17).

quote: A greater number were executed than thrown into prison; indeed, the multitude of men and women who suffered in both ways, was very considerable.
notes: Those guilty of debauchery, murder, or fraud under the Bacchanalian oath are put to death en masse, condemned women handed to relations for private execution (livy:en:39:18).

quote: the senate passed a decree, that no Bacchanalian rites should be celebrated in Rome or in Italy
notes: The senatus consultum de Bacchanalibus permanently bans the rites save by senatorial licence with no more than five worshippers, no common fund, and no priest (livy:en:39:18).

quote: the city quaestors should give to each of them, out of the public treasury, one hundred thousand asses
notes: Senate and commons vote money, military exemption for Aebutius, and unprecedented legal privileges for the freedwoman Fecenia, institutionalizing the informer-reward machinery (livy:en:39:19).

quote: he had found two colonies deserted, Sipontum on the upper sea, and Buxentum on the lower
notes: On the consul's report of two deserted colonies, the senate appoints commissioners to conduct new settlers to Sipontum and Buxentum (livy:en:39:23).

quote: During that year there was a formidable insurrection of the slaves in Apulia.
notes: A slave and shepherd conspiracy infesting roads and pastures around Tarentum is crushed by the praetor, who condemns some seven thousand (livy:en:39:29).

quote: Claudius, the consul, unattended by his lictors, canvassed with his brother through all parts of the forum
notes: Consul Appius Claudius flouts propriety by canvassing for his brother; tribunician contentions repeatedly interrupt the election before Publius Claudius wins against expectation (livy:en:39:32).

quote: He gave a charge to Onomastus, who had the command of the sea-coast, to put to death the leaders of the opposite party.
notes: Macedonian polity: ordered to free Maronea, Philip instead has the pro-Roman leaders massacred and poisons Cassander rather than surrender him to senatorial examination (livy:en:39:34).

quote: as every thing was directed by passion, not by reason, they were condemned to die
notes: Achaean polity: the general council, inflamed against the restored Spartan exiles Areus and Alcibiades for their embassy to Rome, condemns them to death (livy:en:39:35).

quote: Nothing more was done, only the sentence lately passed on Areus and Alcibiades was reversed.
notes: Achaean polity: after Lycortas' defiant defence of Achaean sovereignty, Appius Claudius' veiled threat compels reversal of the death sentence on the Spartan appellants to Rome (livy:en:39:37).

quote: The former threatened, if the senate voted for bringing home the armies, to protest against their decree
notes: Tribunes and consuls line up on both sides over discharging the Spanish armies, trading veto threats until a compromise decree on recruitment and discharge passes (livy:en:39:38).

quote: The senate therefore gave their judgment, that the present number of praetors was sufficient
notes: The curule aedile elect Fulvius Flaccus obstinately stands for a vacant praetorship against the consul and senate, who finally abandon the by-election altogether (livy:en:39:39).

quote: in spite of the opposition made by the nobility, they not only made Marcus Porcius censor, but gave him for his colleague Lucius Valerius Flaccus
notes: The combined nobility fails to block Cato, who campaigns on menaces of a severe censorship and carries Valerius Flaccus in with him (quote at livy:en:39:41; candidacies in 39:40).

quote: If we are to credit Valerius Antias, he condemned about two thousand men.
notes: The praetor Naevius is detained four months by inquisitions into poisonings held through the corporate towns, with some two thousand condemned per Antias (livy:en:39:41).

quote: punished numerous conspiracies of the peasants, and, with great care, finished the remainder of the inquiries concerning the Bacchanalians
notes: The praetor of Tarentum completes the residual Bacchanalian inquisitions, executing some fugitives from bail and remanding others to prison at Rome (livy:en:39:41).

quote: they expelled seven from the senate, one of them a man of consular rank, highly distinguished by nobility of birth and honourable employments
notes: Cato's censorial review expels seven senators, above all the consular Lucius Quinctius Flamininus for killing a Gaul at dinner to amuse his favourite (quote at livy:en:39:42; Antias variant in 39:43).

quote: In the review of the knights, Lucius Scipio Asiaticus was degraded.
notes: In the equestrian review the censors strip Lucius Scipio Asiaticus of his horse, extending Cato's campaign against the Scipionic circle (livy:en:39:44).

quote: They farmed out the several branches of the revenue at the highest prices, and bargained with the contractors for the performance of the public services on the lowest terms.
notes: Cato's censorship taxes luxury tenfold, reclaims public water and ground, builds the Basilica Porcia, and defies senate revocation of the tax-farming contracts by re-letting them (livy:en:39:44).

quote: two colonies were established, Potentia in Picenum, and Pisaurum in the Gallic territory. Six acres were given to each settler.
notes: Citizen colonies are planted at Potentia and Pisaurum with six acres per settler under a single board of commissioners (livy:en:39:44).

quote: disturbances still subsisted, in consequence of the old quarrels, and Messene had revolted from the Achaean confederacy
notes: Greek polity: Messene secedes from the Achaean confederacy, a revolt ultimately crushed and reversed after war (quote at livy:en:39:48; outcome in 39:50).

quote: The party that were more eager for his immediate execution, at length prevailed, and a person was sent to him with poison.
notes: Messenian polity: the captured Achaean praetor Philopoemen is imprisoned in the public treasury and poisoned by the revolt's leaders against popular sentiment; Messene later surrenders the guilty (quote at livy:en:39:50; capture in 39:49).

quote: The present generation have sent an ambassador, of consular rank, to persuade Prusias villanously to murder his guest.
notes: Roman political side of Hannibal's death: Flamininus' embassy to Prusias precipitates the guarding of Hannibal's house and his suicide by poison (livy:en:39:51).

quote: though neither banished nor condemned, yet under prosecution, and summoned as an absent criminal to a trial, at which he did not appear, passed sentence of voluntary exile
notes: Livy dates Scipio Africanus' death from his prosecution by the tribune Naevius: still under charge, he dies in self-imposed exile refusing burial at Rome (livy:en:39:52).

quote: Fear tortured Perseus, lest his age alone might not sufficiently secure his interest, his brother having the advantage of him in every other particular
notes: Macedonian polity: Demetrius' Roman favour breeds envy in Perseus and suspicion in Philip, the dynastic intrigue that will destroy Demetrius (quote at livy:en:39:53; senate's honouring of Demetrius in 39:47-48).

quote: They sent ambassadors to Rome to complain of those proceedings, who being introduced to an audience of the senate
notes: Disarmed Gallic settlers appeal to the senate, which orders their property restored provided they recross the Alps and warns the Gallic states (livy:en:39:54).

quote: In the same year, colonies of Roman citizens were led out to Mutina and Parma.
notes: The senate debates Latin versus citizen status for Aquileia, deciding for a Latin colony, while citizen colonies go out to Mutina, Parma, and Saturnia (livy:en:39:55).

quote: seizing and confining the sons of those whom he had destroyed, and sending them out of the world at different times
notes: Macedonian polity: Philip, amid popular hatred over forced coastal transplantations, resolves to seize and kill the sons of nobles he had executed (livy:en:40:3).

quote: she would kill them all with her own hand, rather than they should come into the power of Philip
notes: Macedonian polity: Theoxena kills her sons and herself fleeing Philip's seizure order against children of the executed Herodicus line (livy:en:40:4).

quote: no hope was left him of obtaining the crown save by the instrumentality of some wicked device
notes: Macedonian polity: Perseus, fearing Demetrius's popularity and Roman favor, begins suborning Philip's friends against his brother (livy:en:40:5).

quote: I, the most unhappy of fathers, sit here as judge between my two sons, the accuser and the accused of the crime of fratricide
notes: Macedonian polity: Philip sits in judgment between Perseus (accuser) and Demetrius after the night brawl; hearing spans chs. 8-15 and Philip defers a verdict; quote at livy:en:40:8.

quote: the senate therefore ordered the new praetor to cut up that evil by the roots, lest it might spread again more extensively
notes: Senate assigns the praetor of Apulia renewed inquisition into surviving Bacchanalian cells, the sequel to the 186 conspiracy suppression (livy:en:40:19).
