quote: The consuls, also, by direction of the senate, proposed to the people certain laws concerning canvassing for elections.
notes: Consuls carry laws de ambitu (electoral canvassing) at the senate's direction (livy:en:40:19).

quote: produced to the king a forged letter, sealed with a counterfeit seal of Titus Quintius
notes: Macedonian polity: Perseus's agents betray Demetrius's planned flight and produce a letter forged under Flamininus's seal; Demetrius's friend Herodotus dies under torture (livy:en:40:23).

quote: It is said that poison was administered to him in that supper.
notes: Macedonian polity: on Philip's secret order Didas poisons and then suffocates Demetrius at Heraclea - the judicial murder closing Perseus's conspiracy (livy:en:40:24).

quote: The year was rendered remarkable by a drought, and a scarcity of the productions of the earth.
notes: Six rainless months produce drought and crop scarcity; no political remedy recorded (livy:en:40:29).

quote: The colony of Gravisca was established this year in a district of Etruria, formerly taken from the Tarquinians
notes: Citizen colony of Gravisca planted on confiscated Tarquinian land, five iugera per settler, under three commissioners (livy:en:40:29).

quote: the senate decreed, that the praetor's having offered his oath ought to be deemed sufficient evidence that those books should, without delay, be burned in the comitium
notes: Alleged books of Numa (Pythagorean doctrines) dug up on the Janiculum; after tribunician appeal the senate orders the urban praetor to burn them publicly as subversive of state religion (livy:en:40:29).

quote: In the same year the Latin colony of Aquileia was established in the Gallic territory.
notes: Latin colony of Aquileia settled with 3,000 infantry allotments of fifty iugera each under three commissioners (livy:en:40:34).

quote: they would either leave it without orders, or, if any one would attempt to detain them by compulsion, would break out into a dangerous mutiny
notes: Veterans of the Spanish army demand discharge, threatening mutiny; Gracchus contests stripping his province of troops and the senate brokers a phased discharge (livy:en:40:35, settled in 40:36).

quote: to make inquisition concerning acts of poisoning committed in the city, or within ten miles of it
notes: Quaestio de veneficiis decreed amid the pestilence; the consul Piso's death is laid to his wife Quarta Hostilia, who is condemned after witnesses tie it to her son's consular ambitions (livy:en:40:37).

quote: These were the first who ever triumphed without having fought an enemy.
notes: Precedent-setting honor: Cornelius and Baebius triumph for the bloodless transplantation of 40,000 Apuan Ligurians to Samnium (livy:en:40:38).

quote: a decree was passed that Marcus Fulvius should be banished into that part of Spain beyond New Carthage
notes: Military tribune Fulvius Nobilior illegally disbands his legion; the senate banishes him beyond New Carthage, docks the legion half a year's pay, and orders deserters sold (livy:en:40:41).

quote: a fine was therefore imposed on him by the pontiff; and when the latter appealed, they contended about the affair before the people
notes: Chief pontiff fines duumvir Dolabella for refusing to resign for inauguration as rex sacrorum; popular vote is broken off by an omen and the pontiffs consecrate Claelius instead (livy:en:40:42).

quote: he had already passed sentence on three thousand people
notes: Praetor Maenius reports 3,000 condemnations in the extended inquisition into sorceries/poisonings beyond the tenth milestone, with cases still multiplying (livy:en:40:43).

quote: a law was proposed by Lucius Villius, plebeian tribune, ascertaining at what ages men might sue for, and hold each office in the state
notes: Lex Villia annalis fixes minimum ages for the magistracies, instituting the formal career ladder; the family earns the surname Annalis (livy:en:40:43).

quote: To the Pisans, offering ground for the establishment of a Latin colony, thanks were returned by the senate, and triumvirs were appointed
notes: Senate accepts Pisan land for a Latin colony (the later Luna) and names three commissioners (livy:en:40:43).

quote: no greater sum should be expended on the games than that which had been voted to Fulvius Nobilior
notes: Senate caps spending on Fulvius's votive games, reacting to the burdensome exactions of Ti. Sempronius's aedilician games (livy:en:40:44).

quote: Apparent hostilities existed between these men, which were frequently displayed in many violent disputes, both in the senate and in the assemblies of the people.
notes: Bitter personal enemies Lepidus and Fulvius Nobilior elected censors together; Metellus leads the principes in a public mediation that forces their reconciliation (livy:en:40:45, speech in 40:46).

quote: They likewise made an alteration in the mode of voting
notes: Censors expel three senators, reclaim occupied shrines, establish port dues, and reorganize tribal voting by rank and calling (livy:en:40:51).

quote: petitioned the consul and senate for some land, that they might live as peaceable subjects, under the government of the Roman people
notes: Three thousand Transalpine Gauls peacefully appeal to consul and senate for land; the senate expels them from Italy and orders those who prompted the migration punished (livy:en:40:53).

quote: disclosed the whole process of the villany of the ambassadors, and his own services therein
notes: Macedonian polity: Xychus, confronted with torture, confesses the forging of the Flamininus letter; Philocles is seized, Apelles flees to Italy, Philip's remorse doubles (livy:en:40:55).

quote: I am resolved to transfer to you the kingdom which I received from your uncle
notes: Macedonian polity: the remorseful Philip tries to divert the succession from Perseus to Antigonus, touring Macedonian cities to commend him, but dies before effecting it (livy:en:40:56).

quote: seized on the throne, which was obtained by wickedness
notes: Macedonian polity: the physician Calligenes conceals Philip's death until Perseus arrives and seizes the kingship ahead of Antigonus (livy:en:40:57).

quote: Perseus, having got possession of the kingdom, ordered Antigonus to be put to death
notes: Macedonian polity: the new king Perseus eliminates his rival Antigonus, then sends envoys to Rome to renew the treaty and seek the royal title (livy:en:40:58).

quote: extraordinary levies were ordered by proclamation, both in the city and throughout all Italy
notes: False report brought by Aquileian fugitives that the camp was taken and the whole army cut off caused panic at Rome and emergency tumultus levies, halted when Junius's letter revealed the army was safe (livy:en:41:5).

quote: Against this proposition, Quintus Aelius, another tribune, protested; and, after violent struggles, prevailed so far, as to prevent its being passed
notes: Tribunes proposed ending Manlius's prorogued command at the ides of March so he could be tried for his unauthorized Istrian war, but a colleague's veto blocked the bill (livy:en:41:6).

quote: The plebeian tribunes, Papirius and Licinius, after harassing him in the senate, with questions relative to what had passed in Istria, brought him into the assembly of the people
notes: Tribunes interrogated consul Junius before senate and people over the Istrian debacle and demanded Manlius answer as a private citizen for waging war without senate or popular authorization; no trial outcome recorded (livy:en:41:7).

quote: their citizens, having been rated in the general survey at Rome, had most of them removed thither
notes: Embassies of the Latin confederate states, Samnites and Pelignians complained to the senate that fraudulent migration and fictitious manumission were draining their citizen rolls and levy capacity; the senate granted their petitions (livy:en:41:8).

quote: Caius Claudius, by direction of the senate, proposed a law and issued a proclamation
notes: Law and proclamation ordered allies surveyed as Latins since the censorship of Marcus Claudius and Titus Quintius to return to their states by the calends of November, with a senate decree imposing an anti-fraud oath at manumissions (livy:en:41:9).

quote: he summoned the person who acted as quaestor to Manlius, and ordered him to bring fetters, threatening to send Junius and Manlius to Rome in chains
notes: Consul Claudius, arriving in Istria without vows, lictors or military habit, was refused obedience by the proconsuls, the quaestor and the jeering soldiery, and had to return to Rome to take up his command in due form (livy:en:41:10).

quote: The same year a colony of two thousand Roman citizens was settled at Luca
notes: Citizen colony planted at Luca by triumvirs on land taken from the Ligurians, fifty-one and a half acres per settler (livy:en:41:13).

quote: they followed his chariot in silence to show their disgust
notes: Allied troops, given only half the donative of citizen soldiers at Caius Claudius's double triumph over Istria and Liguria, staged a silent protest in the procession; coded riot-tumult as nearest category for collective soldier protest (livy:en:41:13).

quote: An interregnum, therefore, took place, and the interrex elected consuls Publius Mucius Scaevola, and Marcus Aemilius Lepidus
notes: After both regular consuls died (Petillius in battle, Cornelius by sickness), experts in religious and political rules held the substituted consuls could not preside at elections, forcing recourse to an interregnum (livy:en:41:18).

quote: Scipio struggled hard to be admitted even in the last place, yet he was thought to have degenerated so far from the virtues of his father
notes: Invidious praetorian election struggle in which Cicereius, his father's former secretary, was outpolling Africanus's son but withdrew his candidacy to let Scipio win; passage may lie partly in supplemented text (livy:en:41:20).

quote: When the termination of the plague was not visible, the senate voted that the decemvirs should consult the Sibylline books
notes: Great pestilence killed priests and slaves, obstructed the consular levies, and was met with Sibylline consultation, supplication and a public vow dictated in the forum; coded famine-scarcity as nearest category for a mortality crisis, hence low confidence (livy:en:41:21).

quote: The remarkable censures pronounced were on Marcus Cornelius Maluginensis, who had been praetor in Spain two years before
notes: Strict censorship of Fulvius Flaccus and Postumius expelled nine senators including a sitting praetor and the censor's own brother and unhorsed many knights; coded prominent-trial as nearest category for censorial nota, not a judicial proceeding (livy:en:41:27).

quote: Marcus Cato put an end to all hesitation, having been already, on a former occasion, a most determined adversary and reprover of women
notes: Hotly debated tribunician law of Voconius Saxa barring women as heirs and capping female inheritances and legacies was carried after Cato's speech against wealthy matrons (livy:en:41:28).

quote: after a violent struggle in consequence of the great number of candidates
notes: Consular elections were carried only after a violent struggle among many candidates; competitive contest within ordinary channels, so confidence low as a coded conflict event (livy:en:41:28).

quote: The resentment of the consul, which, even if well founded, ought not to have been exerted during his office
notes: Consul Postumius's unprecedented demands on Praeneste created a de facto new institution of magisterial exactions from allies (quote at livy:en:42:1).

quote: a contract should be entered into for carrying the tiles back to the temple, and that atonements should be offered to Juno
notes: Senate collectively censured censor Fulvius Flaccus for stripping the temple of Juno Lacinia and decreed restitution and expiation, an accountability proceeding short of a formal trial (quote at livy:en:42:3).

quote: They apportioned ten acres to each Roman, and three to each Latin colonist.
notes: Senate decreed viritane distribution of conquered Gallic and Ligurian land through a ten-man commission, settlement rather than a formal colony (quote at livy:en:42:4).

quote: The Aetolians were not the only people in a state of distraction, on account of the intolerable burden of their debts
notes: Non-Roman polities (Thessaly, Perrhaebia, Aetolia): debt unrest settled extraordinarily by Roman envoy Appius Claudius, who cancelled usurious accumulations and scheduled payments (quote at livy:en:42:5).

quote: the senate ordered, that the consul, Marcus Popilius, should reinstate the Ligurians in their liberty, repaying the purchase-money to the buyers
notes: Opening phase of the Popillius scandal: senate condemned the enslavement of the surrendered Statellates and ordered restitution, which the consul ignored (quote at livy:en:42:8).

quote: The consul exerted the same ferocious spirit in disobeying the senate, which he displayed towards the Ligurians
notes: Popillius returned to Rome, demanded cancellation of the decree and threatened to fine the praetor, producing an unresolved consul-senate standoff rather than a formal veto (quote at livy:en:42:9).

quote: by giving notice, that if they would pass any vote on the subject he would enter his protest, he deterred him from proceeding in the matter
notes: New consul Popillius blocked renewal of the Ligurian decree by threatened protest, and the senate retaliated by withholding Macedonia, levies and reinforcements (quote at livy:en:42:10).

quote: being desirous of commencing the war with his bloodshed, he suborned Evander, a Cretan, commander of the auxiliaries, and three Macedonians
notes: Non-Roman polity (Macedon/Delphi), coded per instruction: Perseus's suborned assassins ambushed King Eumenes at Delphi, who barely survived (quote at livy:en:42:15).

quote: to procure poison to be given to such of them as he should point out by letter
notes: Perseus pressed the Brundisian host Rammius to poison Roman commanders; the informer was brought before the senate, hardening the judgment of Perseus as an enemy (quote at livy:en:42:17).

quote: Marcus Lucretius, plebeian tribune, published a proposal for an order of the people, that the censors should let the Campanian land to farm
notes: After Postumius's survey recovered usurped Campanian public land, a tribunician rogation directed the censors to lease it, reversing decades of private encroachment (quote at livy:en:42:19).

quote: two plebeian tribunes, Marcus Marcius Sermo and Quintus Marcius Sylla, declared publicly that they would institute a suit for a fine to be laid on the consuls
notes: Tribunes threatened fines against the dilatory consuls and carried a plebiscite mandating freedom for the Statellates and an inquiry entrusted to the praetor Licinius (quote at livy:en:42:21).

quote: Thus was the order of the people, respecting the Ligurians, eluded by artifice
notes: Popillius was twice tried under the Marcian law but the praetor's adjournment let him escape judgment, even as thousands of Ligurians were freed and given land beyond the Po (quote at livy:en:42:22).

quote: the consul did not receive a favourable hearing from the senate, when he spoke in the temple of Bellona of his acts among the Ligurians
notes: Consul Popillius returned late for the elections against senate instruction and was heckled over his brother's Ligurian victims before Licinius and Cassius were elected (quote at livy:en:42:28).

quote: the military tribunes should not be created by their suffrages; but that the consuls and praetors should exercise their judgment and discrimination in their selection
notes: For the Macedonian war year the popular election of military tribunes was suspended in favour of selection by consuls and praetors, an unusual institutional change (quote at livy:en:42:31).

quote: Cassius said, that he would select Macedon without casting lots, nor could his colleague, without perjury, abide their determination
notes: Cassius contested the allotment of Macedonia by invoking his colleague's old oath, but the senate ordered the lot, which gave Macedonia to Licinius (quote at livy:en:42:32).

quote: twenty-three of them, who had held the first posts, appealed to the tribunes of the people
notes: Twenty-three former first-rank centurions appealed to the tribunes against reduced ranks in the Macedonian levy, splitting the tribunician college and stalling the levy (quote at livy:en:42:32).

quote: I have received six civic crowns, I have fulfilled twenty-two years of service in the army, and I am upwards of fifty years of age.
notes: Senior centurion Spurius Ligustinus, though entitled to exemption, volunteered for any rank in his famous exemplary speech to the assembly, undercutting the appeal (quote at livy:en:42:34).

quote: The rest of the centurions, dropping the appeal, submissively answered to their names in the levy.
notes: Resolution of the centurions' appeal: Ligustinus was publicly thanked and made first centurion of the first legion, and the rest abandoned their appeal (quote at livy:en:42:35).

quote: Five chiefs of the Aetolians, who were said to be the first persons that turned their backs, were sent to Rome.
notes: Army politics after the defeat at Callinicus: the consul's council blamed the Aetolian allies for the rout and dispatched five of their chiefs (a non-Roman polity's leaders) to Rome (quote at livy:en:42:60).

quote: tell him not to engage in a war with any nation, unless that against which the senate voted that such war should be waged
notes: At livy:en:43:1 Aquileian deputies' appeal reveals consul Cassius has left his province for Macedon, and the senate dispatches three deputies to restrain him from unauthorized war (type fit imperfect: senate discipline of a magistrate triggered by a colony's appeal).

quote: to appoint out of the senatorian order five judges delegate, to try each person from whom the Spaniards might demand back their money
notes: At livy:en:43:2 Spanish envoys' extortion complaints produce early recuperatores proceedings against ex-governors: Titinius acquitted, Furius Philus and Matienus withdraw into voluntary exile amid suspicion the patrons shielded the powerful.

quote: the Roman magistrates should not have the valuation of the corn; nor should they compel the Spaniards to compound for their twentieths
notes: At livy:en:43:2 the senate, after the trials collapse, enacts standing protections for the Spaniards against magistrates' grain-valuation abuses and forced compounding of the twentieths.

groups: offspring of Roman soldiers and Spanish women
quote: they should be settled as a colony at Carteia, on the ocean
notes: At livy:en:43:3 the senate settles over four thousand sons of Roman soldiers and Spanish women as a Latin 'colony of freedmen' at Carteia, resolving their anomalous status.

quote: decreed that the captives who had been sold should be restored to freedom
notes: At livy:en:43:3 the Coroneans, sacked by consul Licinius, appeal to the senate, which condemns its own commander's conduct by freeing the sold captives; this passage falls in the Crevier supplement bridging a manuscript lacuna, though the decree is confirmed at livy:en:43:4.

quote: the senate judged the war made on the Abderites to be unjust, and had directed that all those who were in servitude should be sought out and restored to liberty
notes: At livy:en:43:4 Abderite ambassadors weeping at the senate-house door win a decree condemning praetor Hortensius' storming of Abdera as unjust and ordering the enslaved restored to liberty, while tribunes were already censuring Lucretius daily before the people.

quote: it would still be unjust to condemn, unheard and absent, a man of consular rank
notes: At livy:en:43:5 allied Gallic and Alpine peoples accuse ex-consul Cassius of devastation and mass enslavement; the senate defers any prosecution until his return from Macedon but conciliates the envoys with lavish gifts and embassies.

quote: the instances of pride, avarice, and cruelty, which his countrymen had suffered from the Roman praetor, Caius Lucretius, and were at that very time suffering from Lucius Hortensius
notes: At livy:en:43:7 the crippled Chalcidian chief Miction, carried into the senate on a litter, details the sacrilege, enslavements and billeting abuses of praetors Lucretius and Hortensius, setting up the prosecution at livy:en:43:8.

quote: an assembly of the people being held, every one of the thirty-five pronounced him guilty
notes: At livy:en:43:8 tribunes Juventius Thalna and Aufidius prosecute ex-praetor Lucretius before the people for his conduct in Greece, and all thirty-five tribes condemn him to a fine of one million asses.

quote: the consuls made a complaint to the senate against the plebeians, that even the younger men did not obey their summons
notes: At livy:en:43:14 the levy for Macedon stalls as the young refuse the consuls' summons; tribunes defend the plebs, the senate transfers the levy to the praetors, and the censors impose a sworn levy-oath and recall furloughed soldiers, completing the levy in eleven days.

quote: by fining and seizing the goods of a person who had appealed to a tribune, and by refusing to admit the tribune's right of protesting
notes: At livy:en:43:16 the censors' edict barring former tax-farmers from new contracts drives the publicani to tribune Rutilius, whose protest and annulment bill the censors defy, escalating the deadlock into a capital prosecution.

quote: declared his intention of prosecuting both the censors for treason; and he demanded of Caius Sulpicius, the city praetor, that he would fix a day
notes: At livy:en:43:16 tribune Rutilius prosecutes both censors for treason before the people; Claudius escapes condemnation by only eight centuries after the nobility don mourning and Gracchus swears to share his colleague's exile, whereupon the prosecution collapses.

quote: one thousand five hundred families were enrolled by a decree of the senate
notes: At livy:en:43:17 the senate answers the Aquileians' request (first raised at livy:en:43:1) by enrolling 1,500 additional colonist families under three commissioners to strengthen the exposed frontier colony.

quote: no person should furnish the Roman magistrates with any thing for the use of the war, except what the senate should determine
notes: At livy:en:43:17 ambassadors Popilius and Octavius publish through Greece a senate decree capping magistrates' war requisitions at senate-authorized levels, institutionalizing the accountability measures of the year.

quote: he caused the divers to be privately put to death, together with Andronicus and Nicias
notes: Perseus secretly executes the divers who recovered the Pella treasure plus Andronicus and Nicias to erase witnesses of his panicked orders (livy:en:44:10).

quote: I am convinced that no person, even at the present time, can hear or read such expressions without indignation
notes: Prusias and the Rhodians appeal to the senate to make peace with Perseus; the Rhodians' arrogant mediation offer outrages the senators, who rebuke them by decree in the next chapter (quote at livy:en:44:14).

quote: the senate thereupon decreed that he should be enrolled in the number of their allies
notes: The Macedonian defector Onesimus, who had urged Perseus to keep the Roman treaty, is received by the senate and rewarded with ally status, a house, and Tarentine land (livy:en:44:16).

quote: the censors performed the general survey with more severity than formerly. A great many were deprived of their horses
notes: The censors conduct an unusually severe review, degrading and disfranchising Publius Rutilius, the ex-tribune who had prosecuted them; coded prominent-trial as censorial sanction on a political enemy (livy:en:44:16).

quote: The consuls chosen were, Lucius Aemilius Paullus, a second time, fourteen years after his first consulship
notes: War anxiety dominates the canvass and the senate recalls the consul to hold expedited elections, returning Aemilius Paullus to end the Macedonian war with provinces allotted immediately (livy:en:44:17).

quote: he requested the senate to send commissioners into Macedonia, to review the armies and the fleet
notes: Paullus has the senate dispatch commissioners to audit the state of the armies, fleet, and prior campaigns before he takes command, an institutional check on earlier commanders' conduct (livy:en:44:18).

quote: it was reported that two showers of stones had fallen, one in the territory of Rome, the other in that of Veii
notes: Prodigies (stone showers at Rome and Veii) are expiated with the nine days' solemnity and priestly vacancies filled; coded new-institution for lack of a prodigy-expiation type in the v1 codebook (livy:en:44:18).

quote: They came into the senate-house dressed in mourning, with their hair and beard neglected, holding in their hands branches of olive
notes: Ambassadors of Ptolemy and Cleopatra supplicate the senate against Antiochus's siege of Alexandria, and the senate sends Popilius Laenas to stop the war (livy:en:44:19).

quote: In every circle, and, truly, at every table, there are people who lead armies into Macedonia
notes: Paullus's contio speech asserting the commander's authority against civilian armchair strategists, inviting critics to come to Macedonia or keep quiet; command-assignment politics following his election (livy:en:44:22).

quote: having, by his ambassador Hippias, consented to pay three thousand talents of silver
notes: Perseus, long balking at the cost, finally concludes the alliance with Gentius for 3,000 talents with oaths and hostages, and sends a joint embassy to incite Rhodes against Rome (livy:en:44:23).

quote: that a free state, and a king, were, in their natures, hostile to each other
notes: Perseus's common message to Eumenes and Antiochus urging monarchic solidarity against the republic that conquers kings by means of other kings (livy:en:44:24).

quote: Thus, having manœuvred with each other to no purpose, they gained nothing but disgrace.
notes: Secret Perseus-Eumenes negotiation over 1,000-1,500 talents for neutrality or peace-brokering collapses on Perseus's refusal to pay in advance, each king trying to defraud the other (livy:en:44:25).

quote: he, being a better guardian of his money than of his kingdom, began to descant on the perfidy and savage behaviour of the Gauls
notes: Perseus's refusal to pay the stipulated gold loses him 20,000 Gallic mercenaries under Clondicus who march home; the fiscal failure Machiavelli cites on money not being the sinews of war (quote at livy:en:44:26; sequel in 44:27).

quote: Through the same avarice, he alienated from him king Gentius.
notes: After Gentius imprisons the Roman ambassadors Perperna and Petilius, Perseus recalls the promised 300 talents, cheating his new ally once Gentius is irrevocably committed against Rome (livy:en:44:27).

quote: that his reign might be more secure, he had put to death Plator, and two active men his friends
notes: Illyrian court politics: Gentius murders his brother Plator and Plator's friends to secure his throne and marries Plator's betrothed Etuta; marginal to scope hence low confidence (livy:en:44:30).

quote: He likewise, by a new arrangement, forbade the sentinels to carry their shields when on duty
notes: Paullus institutes camp discipline reforms - silent order transmission through centurions, unarmed sentinels, rotated day guards - followed in 44:34 by his speech that soldiers must obey, not deliberate (quote at livy:en:44:33).

quote: They were now heard by the council in the camp with much greater indignation than at Rome
notes: Rhodian mediation envoys repeat their offensive peace demand at Paullus's camp; some councillors want them expelled unanswered and the consul defers reply fifteen days (livy:en:44:35).

quote: Depart to some other place, that the few of us who are left alive may not be destroyed on your account
notes: After Pydna, Perseus's royal authority collapses: the Amphipolitan assembly shouts him away, his soldiers desert, and he flees to Samothrace with his treasure as Macedonian cities surrender (livy:en:44:45).

quote: he entered the consecrated place without due auspices; and the augurs, on the matter being laid before them, pronounced the appointment improper
notes: The consul Licinius's appointment of the day for assembling his troops was voided by the augurs for faulty auspices, so the Roman legions stayed in the city all year (livy:en:45:12).

quote: complaining that they were dispossessed of their lands by the Roman colonists
notes: Pisan deputies protested dispossession by the colonists of Luna, and the senate resolved the land dispute by sending five boundary commissioners (livy:en:45:13).

quote: that out of the four city tribes, they should openly, in the court of the temple of Liberty, select one by lot
notes: The censors Gracchus and Claudius disputed whether freedmen could be stripped of the suffrage and compromised by confining them all to one city tribe chosen by lot, the Esquiline (livy:en:45:15, dispute begun at livy:en:45:14).

quote: Cneius Tremellius, a tribune, protested against it, because he had not been chosen into the senate
notes: The tribune Tremellius, passed over in the lectio senatus, vetoed the censors' customary request to prolong their term for building contracts (livy:en:45:15).

quote: that Macedonia should be divided into four districts, each of which should have a council of its own
notes: The senate framed the constitutional settlement for conquered Macedon - nominal freedom, dissolution into four republics with councils, halved tribute, and closure of the gold and silver mines to shut out tax-farmers (livy:en:45:18).

quote: he requested a grant of Aenus and Maronea to himself
notes: Roman senators courting Attalus tried to induce him to seek partition of his brother Eumenes' kingdom, but after Stratius's counsel he asked the senate only for Aenus and Maronea (livy:en:45:20, intrigue at livy:en:45:19).

quote: without first consulting the senate, and without acquainting the consuls, of his own sole judgment he proposed to the people the question
notes: The praetor Juventius Thalna tried to rush a declaration of war on Rhodes past the senate straight to the people, and the tribune Antonius blocked it, dragging Thalna from the rostrum (livy:en:45:21).

quote: that they should neither be declared enemies, nor any longer remain in alliance with Rome
notes: After the Rhodian envoys' suppliant appeal and Cato's speech in their favour, the senate ruled Rhodes neither enemy nor ally and stripped it of Lycia and Caria (livy:en:45:25, appeal from livy:en:45:20-24).

quote: the Macedonians should live free; possessing the same cities and lands as before; governed by their own laws
notes: At the Amphipolis convention Paullus and the ten commissioners proclaimed the new constitution - four districts with separate councils, halved tribute, bans on intermarriage and on working the gold and silver mines (livy:en:45:29, elaborated livy:en:45:30 and 45:32).

quote: Aulus Baebius alone was condemned for having lent Roman soldiers as agents in the butchery
notes: In the inquiry before Paullus and the commissioners into the massacre of 550 Aetolian leaders, the Roman commander Baebius alone was condemned for lending soldiers for the killing (livy:en:45:31, massacre reported livy:en:45:28).

quote: instigated them to attend in full numbers, to give their votes, and to take revenge on a haughty and morose commander
notes: Galba, a tribune of the second legion and personal enemy of Paullus, mobilized soldiers resentful over small booty donatives to vote down their own commander's triumph (livy:en:45:35).

quote: When the tribes which were first called in gave a negative to the question, the principal men in the state ran together to the Capitol
notes: The first tribes voted to reject Paullus's triumph after Galba's speech, until the leading men pressured the tribunes to restart the proceedings so Servilius could speak (livy:en:45:36).

quote: all the tribes, when recalled to give their votes, passed unanimously the bill concerning the triumph
notes: Servilius's speech, baring his scars, shamed the soldiers into reversal and the recalled tribes passed the triumph unanimously; Paullus triumphed three days with Perseus led before his chariot (livy:en:45:39, speech at livy:en:45:37-39, triumph and deaths of his sons at livy:en:45:40).

quote: requested the senate to allow the hostages to be ransomed, at any price that should be judged proper
notes: Ambassadors of Cotys of Thrace appealed to the senate to ransom his son and the hostages, and the senate returned them gratis to display Roman dignity (livy:en:45:42).

quote: He further desired that the alliance with him might be renewed
notes: King Prusias came to Rome in person, congratulated the senate, renewed his alliance, sought the disputed Antiochene territory, and commended his son Nicomedes (livy:en:45:44).
